definition_zh: 热浪（指持续数日的异常高温天气，常伴随高湿度与静风）
definition_en: a prolonged period of unusually hot weather, often with high humidity and still air, causing discomfort and sometimes danger
core_image: 街道蒸腾的柏油路上方，空气扭曲如水面，远处热浪像透明波浪般涌来
scene: 气象预报预警说接下来一周气温将远超历史平均。A heat wave has been declared for the region, with temperatures expected to stay above forty degrees for five days.
sceneCN: 这里取第 1 个义项（被官方气象部门宣布、持续数日的异常高温期）；句意为该地区已进入热浪，预计五天内气温都将维持在四十摄氏度以上。

derivatives.zh: 古英语表「热、热度」的名词，引申为温度、辛辣、压力等义
古英语表「波浪」的名词，引申为一段时间的突发事物、情绪波动等
两词合并的拼写形式，多用于新闻标题与非正式文本

senses.title: A declared period of extreme heat
senses.titleCN: 官方宣布的极端高温期
senses.definition: a prolonged spell of unusually hot weather recognized by meteorological authorities
senses.definitionCN: 由气象部门认可的一段持续异常高温天气
senses.example: The city opened cooling centres when the heat wave was officially declared.
senses.exampleCN: 热浪被正式宣布后，该市开设了纳凉中心。
senses.why: The phrase carries an official status because the spell must meet set criteria before it is called a heat wave.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语带有官方性质，因为一段高温必须达到既定标准，才能被称为热浪。

senses.title: A stretch of unusually hot days
senses.definition: several days running where temperatures climb well above the seasonal average
senses.definitionCN: 连续数天，气温持续远超该季节平均水平
senses.example: Last July we lived through a heat wave that broke every local record.
senses.exampleCN: 去年七月我们熬过了打破当地所有纪录的热浪。
senses.why: Wave adds the sense of a rolling event, so the heat is felt as a moving, enveloping blanket rather than a single hot afternoon.
senses.whyCN: wave 带来一种「滚涌而来」的感觉，因此热浪像一张移动的、笼罩的毯子，而不是某个单独的炎热下午。

senses.title: Heat stress in humans or animals
senses.titleCN: 给人畜带来热应激的高温
senses.definition: a period of hot weather that risks heat exhaustion or heat stroke in living things
senses.definitionCN: 一段有使生物发生热衰竭或中暑风险的高温天气
senses.example: Horses were kept in shaded stables throughout the heat wave.
senses.exampleCN: 整个热浪期间，马匹都被关在阴凉的马厩里。
senses.why: The concrete pairing of heat with wave is the object itself, but the reason we care is the stress it puts on bodies.
senses.whyCN: heat 与 wave 这样搭配指的是天气本身，但我们在乎的是它给身体带来的压力。

senses.title: A wave of heat perceived near a source
senses.definition: a visible or felt ripple of hot air rising from a hot surface
senses.definitionCN: 从高温表面升起、肉眼或身体能感知到的热气涟漪
senses.example: You can see the heat wave shimmer above the tarmac at noon.
senses.exampleCN: 正午时分，你能看见柏油路上方蒸腾的热浪。
senses.why: Here wave is used literally of moving air; heat names what the air carries.
senses.whyCN: 这里 wave 指真正流动的空气；heat 则是这股空气携带的东西。

senses.title: A burst of intense heat in a fire
senses.definition: a moving front of high temperature that pushes outward from a fire
senses.definitionCN: 从火场向外推进的一股高温前沿
senses.example: Firefighters retreated when the heat wave from the blaze became unbearable.
senses.exampleCN: 当火场涌出的热浪变得难以忍受时，消防员后退了。
senses.why: In fire safety texts the phrase means something narrower: the tangible front of hot gas ahead of the flames.
senses.whyCN: 在消防文献里，这个短语有更窄的意思：火焰前方那股摸得着的热气前沿。

senses.title: An unusual hot spell in the oceans
senses.definition: a period of unusually warm ocean surface water that disrupts marine life
senses.definitionCN: 一段海面异常升温、干扰海洋生物的时期
senses.example: Coral bleaching has worsened under a persistent marine heat wave.
senses.exampleCN: 珊瑚白化在持续的海洋热浪下愈演愈烈。
senses.why: Climate reports borrow the phrase and move it onto the sea, where heat spreads as a wave through surface waters.
senses.whyCN: 气候报告借用了这个短语，把它搬到海洋上：热量像波浪一样从表层水域向外扩散。

senses.title: A figurative wave of public or social heat
senses.definition: a surge of criticism or protest that spreads through public discussion
senses.definitionCN: 批评或抗议在公众讨论中扩散开来的一段时期
senses.example: The heat wave on social media forced the company to issue an apology.
senses.exampleCN: 社交媒体上的热议浪潮迫使公司发布道歉。
senses.why: Wave means a spreading front, heat means intensity of feeling; the two join for any surge that rolls through public attention.
senses.whyCN: wave 指扩散的前沿，heat 指情感强度；两者合起来描述任何席卷公众注意力的浪潮。

senses.title: A period of heat in an industrial process
senses.definition: a sustained high-temperature stage within a manufacturing cycle
senses.definitionCN: 制造周期中持续高温的一个阶段
senses.example: The steel ingot must survive a heat wave at over one thousand degrees.
senses.exampleCN: 钢锭必须承受超过一千摄氏度的高温段。
senses.why: In technical writing the phrase is stripped of weather meaning and names a controlled phase of high temperature.
senses.whyCN: 在技术写作里，这个短语剥离了天气的意思，转而指制造过程中受控制的一个高温阶段。

intro.en: Heat wave is a compound of two native English words. The first record in print is American, from newspapers in the 1890s. Both halves keep their everyday senses.
intro.cn: heat wave 是两个英语本土词的复合。它最早见诸印刷是在美国报纸上，年代为 19 世纪 90 年代。两部分都保留着日常的词义。

items.en: Hāt meant hot, and the noun heat, formed from it, has carried the sense of high temperature since early English.
items.cn: 古英语 hāt 意为「热的」，由它形成的名词 heat 自古英语早期就表示高温。

items.en: Wafian meant to fluctuate or wave, and the noun wave described rolling motion long before it was applied to periods of weather.
items.cn: wafian 意为「波动」，名词 wave 在用于天气时期之前，早已指滚涌的运动。

items.en: Newspapers in the United States began using heat wave in the 1890s to describe prolonged hot spells.
items.cn: 美国报纸在 19 世纪 90 年代开始用 heat wave 描述持续的高温期。

items.en: The phrase was later adopted as a semi-technical term by weather services, with thresholds set regionally.
items.cn: 后来气象部门把它当作半技术术语采用，并在各地设定了阈值。

items.en: In the twentieth century the phrase spread to oceans, fires, social criticism and industrial processes.
items.cn: 到 20 世纪，这个短语扩展到海洋、火场、社会批评与工业流程中。

note.en: The first group shares the two constituent words; the second group names other ways of talking about prolonged heat.
note.cn: 第一组共享构成这个短语的两个词；第二组是描述持续高温的其他说法。

entries.definition: The first constituent, meaning high temperature or intensity of feeling.
entries.definitionCN: 第一个构成部分，意为高温或情感强度。

entries.definition: The second constituent, meaning a rolling motion or spreading front.
entries.definitionCN: 第二个构成部分，意为滚涌的运动或扩散的前沿。

entries.definition: The same compound written as a single word, common in headlines.
entries.definitionCN: 同一个复合词写成一个词，常见于新闻标题。

entries.definition: A combined measure of temperature and humidity, often reported alongside heat wave warnings.
entries.definitionCN: 温度与湿度的综合指标，常在热浪警报中一并报道。

entries.definition: The top of a wave, illustrating the rolling source of the metaphor.
entries.definitionCN: 波浪的顶部，点明 wave 这个隐喻的源头。

entries.definition: A period of hot weather, less charged with official status than heat wave.
entries.definitionCN: 一段炎热天气，没有热浪那样强烈的官方色彩。

entries.definition: A stationary high-pressure cap that traps hot air beneath it, the meteorological cause of many heat waves.
entries.definitionCN: 把热空气困在下方的静止高压盖，是许多热浪的气象成因。

entries.definition: An old-fashioned phrase for the hottest part of summer, from astronomy not meteorology.
entries.definitionCN: 旧式说法，指夏天最热的那一段时期，来自天文学而非气象学。

entries.definition: A period of warm sunny weather after autumn has started, the opposite season from most heat waves.
entries.definitionCN: 秋天开始后出现的一段温暖晴朗天气，与多数热浪季节相反。

entries.definition: A sudden sharp rise in temperature, which may be short-lived rather than prolonged.
entries.definitionCN: 气温突然急剧升高，可能短暂而非持续。

normalIntro.en: The phrase joins heat, a word for temperature, with wave, a word for rolling motion. The heat moves like a wave across the region.
normalIntro.cn: 这个短语把表示温度的 heat 与表示滚涌运动的 wave 连起来。热量像波浪一样在区域内推进。

normal.en: Imagine a thick blanket of heat rolling over the landscape in slow waves.
normal.cn: 想象一条厚重的热浪毯子，像波浪一样慢慢滚过大地。

normal.en: A shimmer above tarmac is the tiny local version of the big weather event.
normal.cn: 柏油路上方的蒸腾，是这个大型天气事件的缩小版。

normal.en: Both halves are everyday words, so the phrase is easy to split and picture separately.
normal.cn: 两部分都是日常词，因此这个短语很容易拆开、各自想象。

normal.en: The phrase first appeared in American newspapers, so picture a broadsheet from the eighteen-nineties.
normal.cn: 这个短语最早见于美国报纸，所以想象一张十九世纪九十年代的大报。

normal.en: Official services use the phrase, so a declaration often comes with it.
normal.cn: 官方机构使用这个短语，所以它常伴随一纸宣布而来。

abstract.en: A heat wave is a slow burn of the atmosphere, visible in the way it distorts light.
abstract.cn: 热浪是大气缓慢的灼烧，能从它扭曲光线的样子里看见。

abstract.en: The word wave turns static temperature into something that arrives, peaks and leaves.
abstract.cn: wave 这个字把静态的温度变成了有来、有顶、有走的东西。

abstract.en: Extremes of weather become metaphors because they affect every living thing at once.
abstract.cn: 极端天气之所以能成为比喻，是因为它一次就影响所有活着的东西。

examples.en: The heat wave closed public pools and sent dozens of people to hospital.
examples.cn: 热浪关闭了公共泳池，并将数十人送入医院。

examples.en: Cattle were moved into barns when the heat wave stretched into its third week.
examples.cn: 当热浪延续到第三周时，牛被转移进了谷仓。

examples.en: Climate scientists warn that heat waves will grow longer and hotter this century.
examples.cn: 气候科学家警告说，本世纪热浪会变得更长、更热。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「希特 伟夫」——「希特」是热度，「伟夫」是波浪：一波一波的热气来了，就是热浪

root: heat 来自古英语 hāt「热的」，wave 来自古英语 wafian「波动」；1890 年代美国报纸首次将两词搭配用于描述持续高温期，两者均保持日常词义。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from official meteorological declaration to a general hot spell, heat stress on bodies, shimmering air above hot ground, a front of heat in a fire, a warming of the ocean, a public surge of criticism, and a phase of industrial heat.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从官方气象宣布出发，依次走向一般的酷热时期、身体承受的热应激、热地面上方蒸腾的热气、火场的高温前沿、海洋的升温、公众批评浪潮与工业流程的高温段。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: air shimmering above hot tarmac, with a slow rolling front of heat in the distance.
core.cn: 核心意象：柏油路面上方的空气在扭曲，远处有一股缓慢推进的热浪前沿。

branches.en: THE OFFICIAL DECLARATION: meteorologists name and measure the event.
branches.cn: 官方认定：气象学家给这个事件命名并加以测量。

branches.en: HUMANS AND ANIMALS: the wave rolls into inhabited places and puts bodies under stress.
branches.cn: 人与动物：热浪滚进有人的地方，给身体加压。

branches.en: VISIBLE HEAT AND FIRE: the wave becomes visible in shimmer, or becomes deadly near flames.
branches.cn: 看得见的热与火场：热浪要么以蒸腾变形让你看见，要么在火焰附近变得致命。

branches.en: THE OCEAN WAVE: the pattern is borrowed for the sea.
branches.cn: 海洋热浪：这个模式被借来描述海洋。

branches.en: PUBLIC AND INDUSTRIAL WAVES: the word travels further into public criticism and manufacturing.
branches.cn: 公众与工业热浪：这个词又走进社会批评与工业流程。

intro.en: The phrase is a compound of two native English words. Neither half is built from Latin or Greek roots, so affix items are limited to everyday English parts and related compounds.
intro.cn: 这个短语由两个英语本土词合成。两部分都不来自拉丁或希腊词根，因此构词条目仅限于英语日常成分与相关复合。

latinIntro.en: No Latin roots are directly involved in the phrase itself; both heat and wave descend from Old English.
latinIntro.cn: 这个短语本身不涉及拉丁词根，heat 与 wave 都来自古英语。

items.example: The first half of the compound, unchanged in form.
items.exampleCN: 复合词的前半部分，形态未变。

items.meaning: a rolling motion; a spreading front
items.example: The second half, giving the event its rolling quality.
items.exampleCN: 后半部分，给这个事件加上滚涌的质感。

items.meaning: the same phrase written as one word
items.meaningCN: 同一个短语写成一个词
items.example: Headlines prefer the merged form.
items.exampleCN: 新闻标题偏爱合并的写法。

items.example: The adjective from the same root as heat.
items.exampleCN: 与 heat 同根的形容词。

items.example: A modern adjective from the second half.
items.exampleCN: 由后半部分构成的现代形容词。

items.example: Used with many nouns, not just heat.
items.exampleCN: 可与许多名词搭配，不限于 heat。

items.example: The harm a heat wave causes to living things.
items.exampleCN: 热浪给生物造成的危害。

items.example: A metric used in heat wave warnings.
items.exampleCN: 热浪警报里使用的度量。

derivatives.zh: 两词合并拼写，多见于新闻标题
由 heat 加分词构成，义为「与高温有关的」
由 wave 加后缀构成，义为「波浪状的」
由 heat 加前缀与后缀构成，义为「过热的」

definition_zh: 古气候（指地球历史上某一时期的气候状态，通过冰芯、树轮、沉积物等间接证据重建）
definition_en: the climate of a period in Earth's geological past, reconstructed from proxy records such as ice cores, tree rings, and sediment
core_image: 一位地质学家在南极冰芯前工作，冰芯上可见数层不同颜色的年纹，暗示远古时期的冷暖变化
scene: 古气候学家把从格陵兰取回的冰芯切开分层研究。Paleoclimate records from Antarctic ice cores show that carbon dioxide levels rose and fell with global temperatures over the past million years.
sceneCN: 这里取第 1 个义项（由代用证据重建的地球历史时期气候）；句意为南极冰芯中的古气候记录显示，在过去一百万年里，二氧化碳水平随全球气温一同升降。

pos.zh: 名词：古气候；古气候学对象

derivatives.zh: 希腊语 palaios「古老的」构成的前加成分
来自拉丁语 clima「地区、地球坡度」，与希腊语 klima「纬度、地区」同源
名词后加 -logy 构成，义为「古气候学」
名词后加 -ist 构成，义为「古气候学家」

senses.title: Earth's climate in past geological periods
senses.titleCN: 地球历史上某一时期的气候
senses.definition: the state of the atmosphere and oceans during a specific period of Earth's deep past
senses.definitionCN: 地球遥远过去某一时期内的大气与海洋状态
senses.example: Paleoclimate evidence tells us that Antarctica was once covered by forests.
senses.exampleCN: 古气候证据告诉我们，南极洲曾经被森林覆盖。
senses.why: The compound names a specific field: the study of climate when no modern instruments were yet invented.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词为一个专门领域命名：研究现代仪器发明之前的气候。

senses.title: Reconstructed climate from proxy records
senses.titleCN: 由代用记录重建的气候
senses.definition: a climate pattern inferred not from thermometers but from indirect evidence
senses.definitionCN: 不是由温度计而是由间接证据推得的气候模式
senses.example: Scientists use tree rings and pollen to piece together the paleoclimate of the last ten thousand years.
senses.exampleCN: 科学家用树轮与花粉拼凑出过去一万年的古气候。
senses.why: Paleoclimate is never measured directly, so the word always carries the sense of a reconstruction.
senses.whyCN: 古气候永远不能直接测量，因此这个词总带着「重建」的意味。

senses.title: A specific ancient climate state
senses.titleCN: 某一具体的古代气候状态
senses.definition: a particular snapshot of climate at a known geological age
senses.definitionCN: 某一已知地质年代的具体气候快照
senses.example: The mid-Cretaceous paleoclimate was far warmer than anything we know today.
senses.exampleCN: 白垩纪中期的古气候比我们今天所知的任何时期都要暖得多。
senses.why: Used with a date or geological period, the phrase picks out one slice of deep time.
senses.whyCN: 当它后面接一个日期或地质年代时，这个词挑出了遥远时间里的一个切片。

senses.title: Paleoclimate data as a proxy for future risk
senses.titleCN: 作为未来风险参照的古气候数据
senses.definition: old climate data used to test climate models and bound future projections
senses.definitionCN: 用来检验气候模型并约束未来预测的古老气候数据
senses.example: Paleoclimate constraints are essential for predicting how fast sea level may rise.
senses.exampleCN: 古气候约束条件是预测海平面上升速度所必需的。
senses.why: Once reconstructed, paleoclimate becomes a calibration target for the models that forecast our own future.
senses.whyCN: 一旦被重建出来，古气候就变成了那些预报我们未来的模型的校准靶。

senses.title: The field of study that reconstructs ancient climate
senses.titleCN: 重建古代气候的研究领域
senses.definition: a shorthand for the whole discipline of paleoclimatology
senses.definitionCN: 古气候学整个学科的简称
senses.example: Paleoclimate has transformed our understanding of long-term carbon cycles.
senses.exampleCN: 古气候研究改变了我们对长期碳循环的理解。
senses.why: By metonymy the object of study can stand for the whole field that studies it.
senses.whyCN: 通过换喻，研究对象本身可以代表研究它的整个学科。

senses.title: Climate on other planets in the past
senses.titleCN: 其他行星历史上的气候
senses.definition: ancient climate patterns on Mars or other celestial bodies, inferred from remote sensing
senses.definitionCN: 从遥感推断出的火星或其他天体的古代气候模式
senses.example: Evidence of liquid water on Mars hints at a warmer paleoclimate there.
senses.exampleCN: 火星上液态水的证据暗示它曾有过更温暖的古气候。
senses.why: The word was born on Earth, but it travels to other planets when the same kinds of proxy evidence are found.
senses.whyCN: 这个词在地球上诞生，但当其他行星上也发现了同类代用证据时，它就被带了过去。

senses.title: Paleoclimate layers in ice or sediment
senses.titleCN: 冰芯或沉积物中的古气候层
senses.definition: a physical layer in a core that contains paleoclimate information
senses.definitionCN: 冰芯或岩芯中包含古气候信息的物理层
senses.example: Each paleoclimate layer in the Greenland ice sheet records a single year.
senses.exampleCN: 格陵兰冰盖中的每一层古气候都记录了一个年度。
senses.why: The noun names the climate, but it can also name the material object that holds the record of that climate.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词指气候本身，但它也可以指保存该气候记录的那个物理载体。

senses.title: Debate over ancient climate reconstructions
senses.titleCN: 关于古代气候重建的争论
senses.definition: controversies around specific paleoclimate datasets and their interpretation
senses.definitionCN: 围绕具体古气候数据集及其解释的争论
senses.example: That reconstruction of the Last Glacial Maximum paleoclimate has been challenged by other teams.
senses.exampleCN: 那份关于末次冰期最盛期古气候的重建方案遭到了其他研究组的质疑。
senses.why: Science words can also label the disagreements that surround the science.
senses.whyCN: 科学术语也可以用来标记围绕该科学产生的分歧。

intro.en: Paleoclimate is a compound of two borrowings: paleo-, from Greek palaios meaning old, and climate, from Greek klima meaning region or latitude. The first recorded English use as a technical term was in the 1920s.
intro.cn: paleoclimate 是两个外来成分的复合：前半来自希腊语 palaios「古老的」，后半来自希腊语 klima「地区、纬度」。它作为技术术语的最早英文记录在 1920 年代。

items.en: Paleoclimate first appeared as a technical English term in 1922, used to describe climate of earlier geological periods.
items.cn: 1922 年它首次作为技术术语在英语中出现，用于描述较早地质时期的气候。

items.en: Palaios meant old or ancient; the combining form paleo- is used for anything very old.
items.cn: palaios 意为「古老的」；它的组合形式 paleo- 用来指任何很老的东西。

items.en: Klima meant latitude or region, from the root klinein to incline, as in the slope of the earth.
items.cn: klima 意为「纬度、地区」，来自表示「倾斜」的词根 klinein，指地球的坡度。

items.en: Latin borrowed clima and passed it into Old French as climat, which came to English as climate.
items.cn: 拉丁语借用 clima，传入古法语成为 climat，再进入英语成为 climate。

items.en: The compound paleoclimate was built within the sciences of the early twentieth century, not inherited from older usage.
items.cn: paleoclimate 这个复合词是 20 世纪初在科学内部造出来的，不是从旧用法传承下来的。

items.en: By the second half of the century it was widely used across geology, biology and planetary science.
items.cn: 到世纪下半叶，它已广泛用于地质学、生物学与行星科学。

note.en: The first group shares the combining form paleo- or the noun climate; the second group names related kinds of climate study.
note.cn: 第一组共享 paleo- 这个组合形式或 climate 这个名词；第二组是相关气候研究的类别。

entries.definition: The modern climate of the present day, not the past.
entries.definitionCN: 指当代的现代气候，而不是过去的。

entries.definition: The Greek-derived combining form meaning old or ancient.
entries.definitionCN: 来自希腊语的组合形式，意为「古老的」。

entries.definition: The full name of the discipline that studies paleoclimate.
entries.definitionCN: 研究古气候的学科全名。

entries.definition: Another discipline beginning with paleo-, here the study of fossils and ancient life.
entries.definitionCN: 同样以 paleo- 开头的另一门学科，这里指研究化石与古代生命的古生物学。

entries.definition: The Greek word meaning old, from which paleo- is built.
entries.definitionCN: 希腊语中意为「古老的」的词，paleo- 即从中而来。

entries.definition: A plain English phrase with the same broad meaning, less technical than paleoclimate.
entries.definitionCN: 意思相近的普通英文短语，不如 paleoclimate 那么技术化。

entries.definition: Climate of the past inferred from fossil organisms and their distributions.
entries.definitionCN: 从生物体化石及其分布推得的古代气候。

entries.definition: Climate of the very distant past, emphasizing the geological timescale.
entries.definitionCN: 指非常遥远过去的气候，强调地质时间尺度。

entries.definition: Climate within human written history, a much narrower slice than paleoclimate.
entries.definitionCN: 人类有文字历史时期的气候，时间范围远小于古气候。

entries.definition: A climate reconstruction derived from indirect indicators, not the climate itself.
entries.definitionCN: 由间接指标推得的气候重建结果，而非气候本身。

normalIntro.en: The word is paleo- for old, climate for climate. Think of a thermometer buried in a million-year-old ice core.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词前半是「古老的」，后半是「气候」。想象一根温度计埋在百万年的冰芯里。

normal.en: Break it into paleo- (old) and climate (weather pattern).
normal.cn: 拆成两部分记：paleo- 是「古老的」，climate 是「气候」。

normal.en: Antarctica had forests once — that is a paleoclimate fact.
normal.cn: 南极洲曾经有森林——这是一条古气候事实。

normal.en: The ice core in your textbook is the physical evidence of paleoclimate.
normal.cn: 你教科书里那根冰芯就是古气候的实物证据。

normal.en: The first recorded use of the word is 1922, so picture a laboratory of the nineteen-twenties.
normal.cn: 这个词最早记录在 1922 年，所以想象一间二十世纪二十年代的实验室。

normal.en: The root palaios means old; the root klima means slope of the earth.
normal.cn: 词根 palaios 意为「古老的」，词根 klima 意为「地球的坡度」。

abstract.en: Paleoclimate is a diary of the planet written in ice and dust.
abstract.cn: 古气候是这个星球写在冰和尘土里的一本日记。

abstract.en: Studying paleoclimate is learning to read a language the planet writes over thousands of years.
abstract.cn: 研究古气候就是学习读懂这个星球用几千年来写的一门语言。

abstract.en: The past climate is the only planet we have actually visited on foot; the future is still a forecast.
abstract.cn: 过去的气候是我们唯一真正用脚步走过的那颗星球；未来的气候还只是预报。

examples.en: Paleoclimate data from lake beds shows how dry the Mediterranean became during past ice ages.
examples.cn: 湖床中的古气候数据显示，地中海在过去冰期时变得有多干。

examples.en: Climate models are tested against paleoclimate reconstructions before they are used to forecast the future.
examples.cn: 气候模型在用于预报未来之前，要先用古气候重建结果来检验。

examples.en: The discovery of ancient palm fossils near the poles changed assumptions about paleoclimate.
examples.cn: 极地附近发现远古棕榈化石，改变了人们对古气候的假设。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「佩里奥 克莱迈特」——「佩里奥」就是古老的，「克莱迈特」就是气候，合起来就是古老的气候

root: 希腊语 palaios「古老的」与希腊语 klima「纬度、地区（来自 klinein「倾斜」）」；前者经 paleo- 进入科学英语，后者经拉丁语 clima 与古法语 climat 进入英语成为 climate。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses range from past geological climate itself, to climate reconstructed from proxies, to specific ancient climate states, to its role as a calibration for future forecasts, to the whole discipline, to climates on other planets, to physical layers in cores, and to debates around specific reconstructions.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从地质历史时期的气候本身出发，依次走向由代用证据重建的气候、具体的古气候状态、作为未来预测校准靶的角色、整个学科、其他行星的古气候、岩芯里的物理层，以及围绕具体重建方案的争论。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a scientist slicing an ice core, revealing annual layers with faint dark stripes.
core.cn: 核心意象：一位科学家正在切开一根冰芯，露出带有隐约暗纹的年层。

branches.en: THE PHYSICAL CLIMATE AND ITS RECONSTRUCTION: the thing itself and the way we recover it.
branches.cn: 真实的古气候与它的重建：事物本身，以及我们恢复它的方法。

branches.en: ONE SLICE OF DEEP TIME: a specific geological period named and studied.
branches.cn: 深时里的一个切片：一个特定地质年代被点名并被研究。

branches.en: THE CLIMATE AS LABORATORY: old data calibrates future forecasts.
branches.cn: 古气候作为实验室：古老数据校准未来预测。

branches.en: THE FIELD BEHIND THE DATA: the discipline that produces all these reconstructions.
branches.cn: 数据背后的学科：生成所有这些重建的整个领域。

branches.en: OTHER WORLDS, OTHER OBJECTS, OTHER DEBATES: the word travels outwards to planets, to physical layers, and to scientific controversy.
branches.cn: 其他世界、其他对象、其他争论：这个词向外走向行星、走向实物层、走向科学争议。

intro.en: Paleoclimate combines a Greek combining form, paleo-, with a Latin-derived noun, climate. Neither piece carries derivational suffixes in this compound; the suffixes appear when the compound itself becomes a root for new terms.
intro.cn: paleoclimate 把希腊组合形式 paleo- 与一个拉丁来源的名词 climate 组合在一起。这个复合词本身不带派生词缀；当它自己再变作词根去造新词时，词缀才出现。

latinIntro.en: The Greek pieces are palaios (old) and klima (region); the Latin side contributed clima, which passes through Old French into English as climate.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语部分是 palaios（古老的）与 klima（地区）；拉丁语贡献了 clima，它经古法语传入英语成为 climate。

items.example: It opens a whole family of ancient-study terms.
items.exampleCN: 它开启了整个「古-」家族术语。

items.example: The root behind the combining form.
items.exampleCN: 这个组合形式背后的词根。

items.structure: English noun from Latin and Greek
items.example: The second half of the compound.
items.exampleCN: 复合词的后半部分。

items.example: The ultimate source of climate.
items.exampleCN: climate 的最终来源。

items.example: Latin borrowing from Greek, passed into French.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语借自希腊，再传入法语。

items.example: Adds the discipline suffix -logy.
items.exampleCN: 加学科后缀 -logy。

items.example: Adds the person suffix -ist.
items.exampleCN: 加表示人的后缀 -ist。

items.example: Common suffix for scientific disciplines.
items.exampleCN: 科学学科常见后缀。

items.example: Suffix for practitioners of a field.
items.exampleCN: 表示某领域实践者的后缀。

derivatives.zh: paleoclimate 加 -logy 构成，义为「古气候学」
paleoclimate 加 -logist 构成，义为「古气候学家」
paleoclimate 加 -ic 构成，义为「古气候的」
paleoclimatology 加 -ical 构成，义为「古气候学的」

definition_zh: 气候重建（指利用冰芯、树轮、沉积岩等代用资料恢复地球过去气候状态的科学过程与结果）
definition_en: the scientific process of inferring past climate states from proxy records such as ice cores, tree rings, and sediment, or the resulting climate description
core_image: 一位科学家在白板上把几条不同来源的代用数据曲线上的温度点连成一条跨越万年的曲线
scene: 实验室里堆满了冰芯切片与花粉载片，研究员正在把各种数据整合成一条统一的温度曲线。Climate reconstruction depends on multiple independent proxy records rather than any single source.
sceneCN: 这里取第 1 个义项（由多种代用资料恢复过去气候状态的科学过程）；句意为气候重建依赖多种互相独立的代用资料，而不是任何单一来源。

pos.zh: 名词短语：气候重建；古气候重建

collocations.zh: 生成一份气候重建方案

derivatives.zh: 来自希腊语 klima「纬度、地区」，经拉丁语与古法语传入英语
来自拉丁语 reconstruere「再建造」，由 re-「再」+ construere「建造」构成
动词 reconstruct 加 -tion 构成，义为「重建」

senses.title: The scientific process of restoring past climate
senses.titleCN: 恢复过去气候的科学过程
senses.definition: the act of inferring past temperature, precipitation and circulation patterns from proxy data
senses.definitionCN: 由代用数据推断过去温度、降水与环流模式的过程
senses.example: Climate reconstruction is one of the main tools scientists use to study long-term climate change.
senses.exampleCN: 气候重建是科学家研究长期气候变化的主要工具之一。
senses.why: Reconstruction names the work of piecing something back together; climate names what is being pieced.
senses.whyCN: reconstruction 指把东西拼回去的工作，climate 则是被拼回去的那个东西。

senses.title: A specific result or dataset from such work
senses.titleCN: 此类工作的具体结果或数据集
senses.definition: a single published description of past climate drawn from one or more archives
senses.definitionCN: 从一种或多种档案中得出、并已发表的一份对过去气候的描述
senses.example: That climate reconstruction spans the last two thousand years at annual resolution.
senses.exampleCN: 那份气候重建以年分辨率涵盖了过去两千年。
senses.why: The noun phrase can name either the act or the product, like many compound scientific nouns.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词短语既能指行为本身，也能指行为的产物，许多科学复合名词都是如此。

senses.title: Reconstruction from a particular proxy type
senses.titleCN: 由某一类代用资料所做的重建
senses.definition: a climate reconstruction built from one category of evidence, such as tree rings or ice cores
senses.definitionCN: 由某一类证据（如树轮或冰芯）构建的气候重建
senses.example: The study presents a climate reconstruction based on oak tree rings from central Europe.
senses.exampleCN: 该研究提出了一份基于中欧橡树树轮的气候重建。
senses.why: Scientists often narrow the phrase by naming the archive that supplies the data.
senses.whyCN: 科学家常通过点明提供数据的档案类型，来收窄这个短语的含义。

senses.title: Reconstruction at a particular time resolution
senses.titleCN: 特定时间分辨率的重建
senses.definition: a reconstruction whose time slices are daily, yearly, century-scale and so on
senses.definitionCN: 时间切片为日、年、百年等不同尺度的重建
senses.example: High-resolution climate reconstruction can pick up short-lived events such as volcanic winters.
senses.exampleCN: 高分辨率气候重建能捕捉到火山冬天这类短暂事件。
senses.why: Resolution matters because some events leave only faint traces that coarse-grained data would miss.
senses.whyCN: 分辨率很重要，因为有些事件只留下粗略数据会漏掉的微弱痕迹。

senses.title: Global or hemispheric synthesis
senses.titleCN: 全球或半球尺度的综合重建
senses.definition: a synthesis that combines many regional archives into a continent-scale or planet-scale view
senses.definitionCN: 把许多区域档案合起来，得出大洲或行星尺度图景的综合工作
senses.example: The new climate reconstruction covers every continent and extends back ten million years.
senses.exampleCN: 这份新的气候重建覆盖所有大洲，并延伸到一千万年前。
senses.why: Regional archives can be stitched into larger syntheses, and the phrase travels up that scale ladder.
senses.whyCN: 区域档案能被缝合成更大的综合，这个短语也随之爬上那个尺度阶梯。

senses.title: Model-data comparison exercise
senses.titleCN: 模型与数据的比对工作
senses.definition: using a climate reconstruction to test or constrain a computer model of past climate
senses.definitionCN: 用气候重建结果来检验或约束过去气候的计算机模型
senses.example: The climate reconstruction rules out several proposed mechanisms for the cooling event.
senses.exampleCN: 这份气候重建排除了好几种关于那次降温事件的解释机制。
senses.why: Once produced, a reconstruction becomes a test bed for explanations, not just a description.
senses.whyCN: 一旦产出，重建就变成了检验解释的试验台，而不只是一个描述。

senses.title: Debate about specific reconstructions
senses.definition: controversies over methods, chronologies or proxy calibrations in climate reconstruction
senses.definitionCN: 气候重建中围绕方法、年代序列或代用校准的争议
senses.example: Critics argue that the climate reconstruction overestimates early Holocene warmth.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者认为这份气候重建高估了全新世早期的温暖程度。
senses.why: Like any active field, climate reconstruction generates disagreements that shape the next round of work.
senses.whyCN: 和任何活跃的领域一样，气候重建也会产生分歧，而分歧又塑造下一轮的工作。

senses.title: Reconstruction of future climate analogues
senses.titleCN: 参照过去重建未来气候
senses.definition: using past climate states as analogues for future warming scenarios
senses.definitionCN: 把过去的气候状态当作未来变暖情景的参照
senses.example: Scientists are using the mid-Pliocene warm period in a climate reconstruction for the future.
senses.exampleCN: 科学家正在把上新世中期暖期当作未来气候重建的参照。
senses.why: The past is not only a thing to recover; it is also a laboratory for imagining what lies ahead.
senses.whyCN: 过去不只是被恢复的对象，也是用来想象未来的实验室。

senses.title: Popular or educational representations
senses.titleCN: 面向大众或教学的重建呈现
senses.definition: visualised or simplified versions of climate reconstructions used for teaching or public communication
senses.definitionCN: 用于教学或公众传播的、可视化或简化了的气候重建版本
senses.example: The museum exhibit uses a climate reconstruction to show how warm the Arctic was three million years ago.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆展览用一份气候重建，展示三百万年前北极有多暖。
senses.why: Public-facing versions strip out the uncertainty and emphasize the main trend.
senses.whyCN: 面向公众的版本把不确定性剥掉，只强调主要趋势。

intro.en: Climate reconstruction is a compound of two older English borrowings: climate, from Greek via Latin and French, and reconstruction, from Latin reconstruere meaning to build again. Reconstruction entered English in the eighteenth century.
intro.cn: climate reconstruction 是两个英语借词的复合：climate 来自希腊语经拉丁语与法语传入；reconstruction 来自拉丁语 reconstruere「再建造」，于十八世纪进入英语。

items.en: Reconstruction first entered English around 1791 as a general term for rebuilding or putting back together.
items.cn: reconstruction 约于 1791 年首次进入英语，指重建或重新拼回一起的一般活动。

items.en: Re- means again, construere means to pile up together, build. The noun reconstruction is built directly on this verb.
items.cn: re- 意为「再」，construere 意为「堆在一起、建造」。名词 reconstruction 就直接由这个动词构成。

items.en: Climate descends from Greek klima, meaning latitude or region, via Latin clima and Old French climat.
items.cn: climate 来自希腊语 klima「纬度、地区」，经拉丁语 clima 与古法语 climat 传入。

items.en: The specific phrase climate reconstruction was coined within earth-science research in the second half of the twentieth century.
items.cn: climate reconstruction 这个特定短语是 20 世纪下半叶地球科学研究内部造出来的。

items.en: As paleoclimatology grew, the phrase spread from specialist papers into textbooks, reports and public outreach.
items.cn: 随着古气候学的发展，这个短语从专业论文走进了教科书、报告与公众传播。

note.en: The first group shares the two constituent words or their immediate family; the second group names neighbouring activities in climate science.
note.cn: 第一组共享两个构成词或它们的近缘词；第二组是气候科学中与之相邻的活动。

entries.definition: The thing that climate reconstruction aims to recover.
entries.definitionCN: 气候重建想要恢复的那个对象本身。

entries.definition: The verb behind reconstruction, to build or put back together.
entries.definitionCN: reconstruction 背后的动词，意为「重建、拼回一起」。

entries.definition: The act of building, from the same Latin root as reconstruction.
entries.definitionCN: 建造的行为，与 reconstruction 同属一个拉丁词根。

entries.definition: To take apart, the opposite of reconstruct, built on the same Latin verb.
entries.definitionCN: 拆开，是 reconstruct 的反义，同样来自那个拉丁动词。

entries.definition: The Latin verb meaning to heap, pile, or build, the ultimate root of construction.
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁语中意为「堆、建造」的动词，construction 的终极词根。

entries.definition: A broader phrase that may include reconstruction as one part of a larger project.
entries.definitionCN: 更宽泛的说法，重建可能只是其中一部分工作。

entries.definition: A narrower phrase focused specifically on how proxy data become temperature curves.
entries.definitionCN: 更窄的说法，专指代用数据如何变成温度曲线这一步。

entries.definition: Running a climate model backwards to see if it reproduces the past, not the same as reconstruction.
entries.definitionCN: 把气候模型倒着跑来检验它能否再现过去，不等同于重建。

entries.definition: The study of climate within written records, a much shorter window than most reconstructions.
entries.definitionCN: 研究有文字记录时期的气候，时间窗比多数重建要短得多。

entries.definition: Assembling raw proxy data, a prerequisite but not the same as full reconstruction.
entries.definitionCN: 整理原始代用数据，是前提但不等同于完整重建。

normalIntro.en: Climate reconstruction joins climate, the weather of a region over time, with reconstruction, the act of putting something back together.
normalIntro.cn: climate reconstruction 把「一个地区长期的天气状况」与「把某物重新拼回去」的动作连在一起。

normal.en: Imagine finding a broken pot and gluing the pieces back to see the whole shape.
normal.cn: 想象找到一只碎了的陶罐，把碎片拼回去看它原本的完整形状。

normal.en: The Latin root struere means to heap or build — reconstruction heaps things together again.
normal.cn: 拉丁词根 struere 意为「堆、建造」，reconstruction 就是把东西再堆起来。

normal.en: Ice cores, tree rings, sediment: all are pieces the scientist glues together.
normal.cn: 冰芯、树轮、沉积物，都是科学家粘回去的碎片。

normal.en: The noun reconstruction entered English in the 1790s; the compound phrase is mid-twentieth-century.
normal.cn: reconstruction 这个名词 1790 年代进入英语，整个复合短语则是 20 世纪中期造的。

normal.en: Resolution matters: yearly data catches short events, century data smooths them out.
normal.cn: 分辨率很重要：年数据捕捉短暂事件，世纪数据则把它们抹平。

abstract.en: To reconstruct past climate is to read a book whose pages are scattered across ice, stone and wood.
abstract.cn: 重建过去气候，就是读一本散落在冰、石头和木头里的书。

abstract.en: Every reconstruction is a best guess stitched from imperfect evidence.
abstract.cn: 每一份重建都是用不完美证据缝起来的一个最佳猜测。

abstract.en: The past is never exactly recovered, but the shape of it becomes clear enough to guide the future.
abstract.cn: 过去永远不能被精确恢复，但它的轮廓会变得足够清晰，足以引导未来。

examples.en: The climate reconstruction shows that the current warming trend began in the late nineteenth century.
examples.cn: 这份气候重建显示，当前的变暖趋势始于十九世纪末。

examples.en: A new climate reconstruction from Greenland ice pushes the record of abrupt climate shifts further back.
examples.cn: 格陵兰冰芯的一份新气候重建，把气候突变的记录又往前推了。

examples.en: The team combined tree rings and lake sediments to produce a climate reconstruction covering the past millennium.
examples.cn: 该研究组结合树轮与湖底沉积物，生成了一份覆盖过去一千年的气候重建。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「克莱迈特 瑞康斯恰克深」——「克莱迈特」是气候，「瑞康斯恰克深」是重建，合起来就是把气候拼回去

root: climate 来自希腊语 klima「纬度、地区」，经拉丁语 clima 与古法语 climat 传入；reconstruction 来自拉丁语 reconstruere（re-「再」+ construere「堆、建造」，词根 struere「堆、建造」），于十八世纪进入英语；整个短语为 20 世纪下半叶地球科学内部造词。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses move from the scientific process of restoring past climate, to the resulting dataset, to reconstructions built from particular proxies, to reconstructions at a given resolution, to hemispheric or global syntheses, to model-data comparisons, to debates around reconstructions, to using past climates as analogues for the future, and to public-facing representations.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从恢复过去气候的科学过程出发，依次走向产出的数据集、由特定代用资料所做的重建、特定分辨率的重建、半球或全球尺度的综合、模型与数据的比对、围绕重建的争论、把过去气候当作未来参照，以及面向公众的呈现。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a half-assembled jigsaw where the pieces are tree rings, ice cores and pollen.
core.cn: 核心意象：一幅拼了一半的拼图，拼块是树轮、冰芯和花粉。

branches.en: THE WORK ITSELF: the process of gluing pieces together.
branches.cn: 工作本身：把碎片粘起来的那个过程。

branches.en: THE PRODUCT: a single named dataset the work produces.
branches.cn: 工作的产物：一份有名字的数据集。

branches.en: RESTRICTED RECONSTRUCTIONS: narrowing by archive type or by time resolution.
branches.cn: 收窄的重建：按档案类型或按时间分辨率来限定。

branches.en: SYNTHESIS AND TESTING: stitching many series together, then testing them against models.
branches.cn: 综合与检验：把多条序列缝在一起，再用模型去检验。

branches.en: DEBATE, ANALOGUES AND PUBLIC USE: reconstructions are argued over, used as future analogues, or simplified for display.
branches.cn: 争论、参照与大众使用：重建会被争论，被当作未来参照，或被简化做展示。

intro.en: Climate reconstruction combines two borrowings: climate from Greek through Latin and French, and reconstruction from Latin reconstruere. The two halves were both already in English before they joined into this scientific phrase.
intro.cn: climate reconstruction 把两个借词组合在一起：climate 来自希腊经拉丁语与法语，reconstruction 来自拉丁语 reconstruere。两部分在组成这个科学短语之前，都已存在于英语中。

latinIntro.en: The Latin contributions are reconstruere from re- and construere, with root struere, and clima from Greek klima.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语贡献了由 re- 与 construere 组成的 reconstruere（词根 struere），以及借自希腊语 klima 的 clima。

definition_en: to be widespread or dominant; to gain victory or control after a struggle or opposition
core_image: 暴风雨后，一棵小树在多棵倒下的大树之间仍然挺立，成为唯一还站着的生命
scene: 辩论的最后一轮，原本分散的反对意见逐渐消散。After a heated exchange, the chairman's view prevail and the new policy was adopted.
sceneCN: 这里取第 1 个义项（经过一番斗争后占了上风并被采纳）；句意为经过激烈争论，主席的观点占了上风，新政策被通过。

senses.title: To win out after opposition
senses.definition: to gain acceptance or victory in a struggle against an alternative or opposing force
senses.definitionCN: 在与其他选择或反对力量的斗争中获得接受或胜利
senses.example: Justice prevail after three years of court hearings.
senses.exampleCN: 三年庭审之后，正义占了上风。
senses.why: The Latin root valere means to be strong, and prae- means before; so prevailing is being strong enough to stand before what opposes you.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 valere 意为「强」，prae- 意为「在……之前」，所以 prevail 就是在反对你的东西面前强到足以站住。

senses.title: To be widespread or common
senses.definition: to be usual or dominant in a place or at a time
senses.definitionCN: 在某个地点或时段内成为通常或主导的状态
senses.example: Cold winds prevail in the mountains through most of the year.
senses.exampleCN: 一年中的大部分时间，山间盛行寒风。
senses.why: A thing that is strong enough to stand without being pushed out becomes the usual thing, so the second sense grows directly from the first.
senses.whyCN: 一件东西强到不会被挤走，就变成了通常的东西，因此第二个义项是从第一个义项直接长出来的。

senses.title: To be stronger than an opponent
senses.definition: to defeat or overcome a specific rival or obstacle
senses.definitionCN: 击败或战胜某个具体的对手或障碍
senses.example: Good will prevail over fear in the end.
senses.exampleCN: 善意最终会战胜恐惧。
senses.why: Here the sense is explicitly comparative: one side is stronger than the other.
senses.whyCN: 这里是明确的比较意义：一方比另一方强。

senses.title: To persuade someone successfully
senses.definition: to use influence to get someone to do what you want
senses.definitionCN: 用影响力让某人做你想让他做的事
senses.example: She prevailed on him to reconsider his resignation.
senses.exampleCN: 她劝他重新考虑辞职。
senses.why: This older sense is now less common; it survives in the phrase prevail on or prevail upon.
senses.whyCN: 这个较旧的义项如今不太常见；主要活在 prevail on / prevail upon 这个搭配里。

senses.title: To be currently in force
senses.definition: to be the rule or pattern that applies at the present moment
senses.definitionCN: 成为当前适用的规则或模式
senses.example: Different regulations prevail in each state.
senses.exampleCN: 每个州适用不同的法规。
senses.why: Something that prevails at the moment is what is in force right now, not what used to be.
senses.whyCN: 此刻 prevail 的东西就是此刻生效的东西，不是过去生效的。

senses.title: To be generally believed or felt
senses.definition: to be the common attitude, belief or feeling of a group
senses.definitionCN: 成为一个群体普遍持有的态度、信念或感受
senses.example: A sense of optimism prevail among the staff.
senses.exampleCN: 员工中普遍弥漫着乐观情绪。
senses.why: Attitudes are not built things like policies, but they still can prevail the way a wind does.
senses.whyCN: 态度不像政策那样是被制定出来的，但它仍然能像风一样盛行。

senses.title: To remain standing after a challenge
senses.titleCN: 经受住挑战后仍然存在
senses.definition: to endure and continue to exist despite attempts to remove or change it
senses.definitionCN: 尽管有人试图消除或改变它，它仍然继续存在
senses.example: The small church prevailed through two wars and a flood.
senses.exampleCN: 那座小教堂熬过了两次战争和一场洪水。
senses.why: This sense emphasizes endurance rather than victory; the thing simply remains when others have fallen.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项强调持久，而不是胜利——别的倒了，它只是还在那儿。

senses.title: To be the main or most important one
senses.titleCN: 成为最主要或最重要的那个
senses.definition: to be the option or factor that matters most out of several
senses.definitionCN: 在若干选项或因素中成为最重要的那个
senses.example: Cost considerations prevailed in the final decision.
senses.exampleCN: 成本方面的考虑在最终决定中占了主导。
senses.why: When several factors compete, prevailing is the same as being the one that actually counts.
senses.whyCN: 当几个因素相互竞争时，prevail 就是那个真正起作用的因素。

intro.en: Prevail comes from Latin praevalere, to be stronger than, from prae- before and valere to be strong. It reached English through Old French prevaloir around the fourteenth century.
intro.cn: prevail 来自拉丁语 praevalere「比……强」，由 prae-「在……之前」和 valere「强」合成。它通过古法语 prevaloir 于十四世纪前后进入英语。

items.en: Prevail first appeared in Middle English around 1300 with the sense to be superior in strength, force or influence.
items.cn: prevail 于 1300 年前后首次在中古英语出现，意为「在力量、势力或影响上更优越」。

items.en: From prae- before + valere to be strong. The Latin verb already carried the sense of being stronger than another.
items.cn: 来自 prae-「在……之前」+ valere「强」。拉丁语动词本身已带有「比另一者更强」的意思。

items.en: French adopted the Latin verb as prevaloir, meaning to predominate or overcome; English borrowed it in its Old French form.
items.cn: 法语把这个拉丁动词借成 prevaloir，意为「占主导、战胜」；英语按古法语形式借入。

items.en: After entering English the verb spread from strength and victory to generality, current force and persuasion.
items.cn: 进入英语后，这个动词从力量与胜利的意思扩展到了普遍性、当前生效和劝说等义项。

items.en: The Latin valere family gives English valid, value, valor, evaluate, valiant and many more.
items.cn: 同一拉丁词根 valere 还生出了英语的 valid、value、valor、evaluate、valiant 等众多词。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin root valere or its immediate relatives; the second group lists verbs close in meaning to the core sense of prevailing.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁词根 valere 或其近缘词；第二组是与 prevail 核心义项相近的动词。

entries.definition: An adjective from the same root, meaning widespread or common.
entries.definitionCN: 来自同一拉丁词根的形容词，意为「普遍的、流行的」。

entries.definition: From valere, meaning legally or logically sound.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 valere，意为「合法的、逻辑上成立的」。

entries.definition: From valere through Old French, meaning brave.
entries.definitionCN: 经古法语来自 valere，意为「勇敢的」。

entries.definition: From valere, meaning to judge the worth of something.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 valere，意为「评价、估价」。

entries.definition: From valere via French, meaning courage or bravery.
entries.definitionCN: 经法语来自 valere，意为「勇气、勇敢」。

entries.definition: To win a great victory, often with fanfare; narrower and more ceremonial than prevail.
entries.definitionCN: 赢得大胜，常伴随声势；比 prevail 更窄、更仪式化。

entries.definition: To have control or power over, without necessarily implying a prior struggle.
entries.definitionCN: 拥有控制权或权力，不一定暗指之前有斗争。

entries.definition: To continue despite difficulty, emphasizing endurance rather than victory.
entries.definitionCN: 尽管困难仍继续，强调持久而非胜利。

entries.definition: To accomplish what was aimed at, narrower in scope than prevail.
entries.definitionCN: 成功做到目标所指之事，范围比 prevail 窄。

entries.definition: To gain an advantage without necessarily becoming the prevailing option long term.
entries.definitionCN: 暂时占得优势，不一定意味着长期成为主导。

normalIntro.en: Think of prevailing as being strong enough to stand in front of what opposes you. The Latin prae- means before, valere means be strong.
normalIntro.cn: 把 prevail 想象成「强到足以站在反对你的东西前面」。拉丁语 prae- 是「在……之前」，valere 是「强」。

normal.en: Break it into prae- (before) and valere (strong): be strong before what opposes you.
normal.cn: 拆成 prae-（在……前）和 valere（强）：在反对你的东西面前要强。

normal.en: A tree that prevail against wind is one that still stands after the storm.
normal.cn: 一棵能 prevailing against 风的树，就是风暴过后还站着的那棵。

normal.en: The family is rich: valid, value, valor, evaluate — all from valere.
normal.cn: 这个家族很兴旺：valid、value、valor、evaluate——全都来自 valere。

normal.en: Prevail entered English around 1300 via Old French prevaloir.
normal.cn: prevail 于 1300 年前后通过古法语 prevaloir 进入英语。

normal.en: Older sense of persuade survives in prevail on someone.
normal.cn: 较旧的「劝说」义项活在 prevail on someone 这个搭配里。

abstract.en: To prevail is to survive the pressure to become something else.
abstract.cn: prevail 就是顶住「被变掉」的压力。

abstract.en: The strongest argument is not always the loudest, but it is the one that prevail in the end.
abstract.cn: 最强的论点不一定最响，但它最终会 prevail。

abstract.en: What prevail in a place is what becomes its air.
abstract.cn: 在一个地方 prevail 的东西，就是变成了那个地方的空气的东西。

examples.en: Good prevailed over evil in the end, but the victory cost dearly.
examples.cn: 善最终战胜了恶，但这次胜利代价很高。

examples.en: Temperate climate prevail over most of the European continent.
examples.cn: 温和气候盛行于欧洲大陆的大部分地区。

examples.en: After a long debate, the committee's original decision prevailed.
examples.cn: 长时间的争论之后，委员会最初的决定占了上风。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「普瑞维尔」——「普瑞」在前，「维尔」强：站在前面还能站住的，就是占了上风

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses grow from winning out after opposition, to being widespread, to defeating a rival, to persuading, to being in force now, to being generally believed, to enduring after challenge, to being the most important factor among several.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从「经过反对后占上风」出发，依次走向「广泛存在」、「击败对手」、「劝说」、「当前生效」、「被普遍相信」、「经受住挑战后仍然存在」与「成为最主要的那个」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a single tall tree still standing in a field where all the others have been blown down.
core.cn: 核心意象：一片被吹倒的树中间，还有一棵高树挺立着。

branches.en: WINNING AFTER OPPOSITION: the core of prevail — one side is stronger.
branches.cn: 经过反对后获胜：prevail 的核心——一方更强。

branches.en: SPREADING THROUGHOUT A PLACE: once something wins, it becomes the usual thing.
branches.cn: 在一个地方扩散：一旦赢了，它就变成通常的东西。

branches.en: PERSUASION: a milder use of strength, applied to minds rather than to armies.
branches.cn: 劝说：力度更柔的一种强，用在人身上而不是军队身上。

branches.en: CURRENT FORCE, COMMON BELIEF, DOMINANT FACTOR: being the one that applies right now or matters most.
branches.cn: 当前生效、普遍信念、主导因素：成为此刻适用的或最重要的那个。

branches.en: ENDURANCE: the thing simply keeps standing when everything around it has fallen.
branches.cn: 持久：周围都倒了，它只是一直站着。

intro.en: Prevail is a single verb built from the Latin prefix prae- and the root valere, to be strong. English suffixes such as -ing, -ed and -ment attach to it later.
intro.cn: prevail 是一个由拉丁语前缀 prae- 与词根 valere「强」构成的单词，后来英语词缀如 -ing、-ed、-ment 再加上去。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root valere is shared by a long family of English words: valid, value, valor, evaluate, valiant, prevalent and others.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根 valere 与一长串英语词共享：valid、value、valor、evaluate、valiant、prevalent 等。

definition_zh: 激增；大量繁殖；迅速扩散（指数增长）
definition_en: to grow or multiply rapidly in number, often by producing many new parts or offspring
core_image: 培养皿里的细菌菌落从几个小点迅速布满整个圆盘，像地图上的城市向外蔓延
scene: 新推出的手机应用一周内下载量暴涨。Free parking apps proliferate whenever a city raises meter fees.
sceneCN: 这里取第 1 个义项（同类事物在短时间内数量迅速增加）；句意为每当一个城市提高路边停车费，免费停车应用就会激增。

pos.zh: 及物/不及物动词：激增；大量繁殖；扩散

senses.title: To increase in number very quickly
senses.definition: to grow in count at a rate that seems explosive
senses.definitionCN: 以看起来像爆炸一样的速度在数量上增长
senses.example: Memes proliferate across social media faster than anyone can keep track of.
senses.exampleCN: 梗图在社交媒体上激增，快到没人能跟得上。
senses.why: The word carries an implicit comparison to biological reproduction, where one cell becomes many.
senses.whyCN: 这个词带有一种隐含的生物学比较：一个细胞变成许多细胞。

senses.title: To reproduce by many new parts or offspring
senses.titleCN: 通过产生新部件或后代来繁殖
senses.definition: to multiply by biological cell division or similar budding growth
senses.definitionCN: 通过生物性的细胞分裂或类似的出芽方式增殖
senses.example: Cancer cells proliferate uncontrollably if untreated.
senses.exampleCN: 如果不治疗，癌细胞会不受控制地增殖。
senses.why: This is the literal biological sense, the origin of the later figurative uses.
senses.whyCN: 这是最字面的生物学义项，后来的比喻用法都从它长出来。

senses.title: To spread into many different forms or places
senses.titleCN: 以不同形式或在不同地方扩散
senses.definition: to appear in many places or under many different guises
senses.definitionCN: 在许多地方出现，或以许多不同面貌出现
senses.example: Fake versions of the app proliferate through download portals.
senses.exampleCN: 这款应用的假版本通过下载门户网站四处扩散。
senses.why: The sense of spreading outward sits beside the sense of growing in count.
senses.whyCN: 向外扩散的义项与数量增长的义项并排存在。

senses.title: To make more of something deliberately
senses.definition: to produce many new instances of something on purpose
senses.definitionCN: 故意地制造大量新实例
senses.example: The government proliferated new agencies without closing the old ones.
senses.exampleCN: 政府增加了许多新机构，却没有关闭旧的。
senses.why: Used transitively, the verb names an intentional act rather than just a natural growth.
senses.whyCN: 作及物动词时，它指的是有意的行为，而不只是自然生长。

senses.title: To grow in variety as well as in number
senses.titleCN: 在种类上和数量上一同增加
senses.definition: to diversify and multiply at the same time
senses.definitionCN: 多样化与数量增加同时发生
senses.example: Flowering plants proliferated during the Cretaceous, filling every ecological niche.
senses.exampleCN: 开花植物在白垩纪大量繁殖，占据了每一个生态位。
senses.why: Some proliferations are not just more of the same, but many new kinds.
senses.whyCN: 有些增殖不是同一种的更多，而是许多新种类。

senses.title: To increase in complexity
senses.definition: to branch into many parts or layers, becoming harder to oversee
senses.definitionCN: 分叉成许多部分或层级，变得难以监管
senses.example: Rules and exceptions proliferate until no one can follow them all.
senses.exampleCN: 规则和例外情况大量增多，直到没人能全部掌握。
senses.why: Growth in number can also be growth in complexity, and the word covers both.
senses.whyCN: 数量增长也可能是复杂度增长，这个词把两者都覆盖了。

senses.title: A sudden appearance of many copies
senses.definition: to arrive all at once in large numbers, suggesting an underlying cause
senses.definitionCN: 突然同时大量出现，暗示背后有一个原因
senses.example: After the leak, copies of the document proliferated across every file-sharing site.
senses.exampleCN: 文件泄漏之后，它的副本在每个文件分享网站上大量涌现。
senses.why: The verb hints that there is some shared source, not just random independent appearances.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词暗示有一个共同源头，而不只是随机、独立地各自出现。

senses.title: To spread a belief or an idea widely
senses.titleCN: 把信念或想法广泛传播
senses.definition: to make an ideology or opinion appear in many different spaces
senses.definitionCN: 让一种意识形态或意见出现在许多不同空间
senses.example: Conspiracy theories proliferate in the gaps left by mainstream silence.
senses.exampleCN: 在主流声音沉默留下的空隙里，阴谋论就会大量涌现。
senses.why: Ideas are not organisms, but they reproduce when people repeat them, so the biological metaphor carries over.
senses.whyCN: 想法不是生物体，但人们重复它，它就会繁殖，因此生物学的比喻就带了过来。

intro.en: Proliferate is a back-formation: the verb was built from the noun proliferation, which itself came from French prolifération. The ultimate roots are Latin proles meaning offspring and ferre meaning to bear or carry.
intro.cn: proliferate 是一个逆构词：这个动词是从名词 proliferation 倒着造出来的；而名词 proliferation 又来自法语 prolifération。最底层的词根是拉丁语 proles「后代」和 ferre「承担、携带」。

items.en: The English verb proliferate was formed in the 1870s by back-formation from the already existing noun proliferation.
items.cn: 英语动词 proliferate 是 1870 年代由已存在的名词 proliferation 逆构出来的。

items.en: The noun proliferation entered English earlier, in the 1850s, borrowed from French prolifération.
items.cn: 名词 proliferation 更早，1850 年代就进入了英语，借自法语 prolifération。

items.en: French built the noun from proliférer to produce offspring, itself from Latin proles offspring + ferre to bear.
items.cn: 法语用 proliférer「产生后代」造了这个名词；proliférer 又来自拉丁语 proles「后代」+ ferre「承担」。

items.en: Proles meant offspring, descendants, or progeny in Latin; it shares a root with the English word progeny.
items.cn: 拉丁语 proles 意为「后代、子孙」，与英语 progeny 同根。

items.en: Ferre meant to bear or carry in Latin, a root that reaches ferry, transfer, refer, infer and many others.
items.cn: 拉丁语 ferre 意为「承担、携带」，同源词包括 ferry、transfer、refer、infer 等许多。

items.en: The biological sense remained dominant through the nineteenth century; only later did the word spread to ideas, documents and rules.
items.cn: 整个十九世纪生物学义项一直占据主导，后来这个词才扩展到想法、文件和规则上。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin roots proles and ferre; the second group lists verbs of increase with overlapping senses.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁词根 proles 与 ferre；第二组是含义部分重叠的表示增加的动词。

entries.definition: The noun from which the verb proliferate was back-formed.
entries.definitionCN: proliferate 这个动词就是从它逆构出来的。

entries.definition: An adjective from the same Latin family, meaning producing many offspring or works.
entries.definitionCN: 来自同一拉丁家族的形容词，意为「多产的」。

entries.definition: Descendants or successors, from Latin proles.
entries.definitionCN: 后代；后继者，来自拉丁语 proles。

entries.definition: From ferre to carry, a transport word built on the same root.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 ferre「携带」，是同一词根上的一个运输类词。

entries.definition: From trans- across + ferre to carry.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 trans-「跨越」+ ferre「携带」。

entries.definition: To increase in number by reproduction, less charged with the biological metaphor than proliferate.
entries.definitionCN: 通过繁殖增加数量，比 proliferate 的生物学意味弱。

entries.definition: To extend over space, without necessarily implying multiplication in number.
entries.definitionCN: 向空间延伸，不必然暗示数量倍增。

entries.definition: To produce offspring, still more directly biological than proliferate.
entries.definitionCN: 产生后代，比 proliferate 更直接偏向生物学。

entries.definition: To increase suddenly and dramatically in number, suggesting an explosion-like jump.
entries.definitionCN: 数量突然急剧增加，暗示像爆炸一样的跳跃。

entries.definition: To appear suddenly and in many places, without necessarily implying a single source.
entries.definitionCN: 突然在许多地方出现，不必然暗示有一个共同源头。

normalIntro.en: Proliferate grows from a Latin pair: proles means offspring, ferre means to bear. So it literally means to bear many offspring.
normalIntro.cn: proliferate 来自两个拉丁词根：proles 是「后代」，ferre 是「承担、生育」。所以它字面意思就是「生出许多后代」。

normal.en: Break it: proles (offspring) + ferre (bear) → bear many offspring.
normal.cn: 拆开记：proles（后代）+ ferre（生育）→ 生出许多后代。

normal.en: Bacteria in a petri dish is the image that fits every sense of the word.
normal.cn: 培养皿里的细菌是能装下这个词每一个义项的最佳画面。

normal.en: Ferre also gives ferry, transfer, refer, infer — all about carrying.
normal.cn: ferre 还生出 ferry、transfer、refer、infer——全都跟「携带」有关。

normal.en: The verb is a back-formation from the 1870s, a fake Latin-sounding coinage from an older noun.
normal.cn: 这个动词是 1870 年代的逆构词，从一个更老的名词倒造出一个听起来像拉丁语的形式。

normal.en: Ideas proliferate the way organisms do, by being copied.
normal.cn: 想法 proliferate 的方式和生物一样：被人复制。

abstract.en: Proliferation is growth without a governing plan.
abstract.cn: 增殖是没有统一规划的生长。

abstract.en: Every new copy looks like a success until you look closer.
abstract.cn: 每个新副本看起来都像一次成功，直到你仔细看。

abstract.en: Growth in number is also growth in the noise around a subject.
abstract.cn: 数量的增长同时也是围绕一个主题的噪音的增长。

examples.en: New online payment systems proliferate faster than regulators can review them.
examples.cn: 新的在线支付系统激增的速度，比监管机构审查它们的速度还快。

examples.en: Weeds proliferate in any patch of soil left untended for a season.
examples.cn: 任何一块一季无人照管的土壤里，杂草都会大量生长。

examples.en: During the pandemic, misinformation about vaccines proliferated across social media.
examples.cn: 大流行期间，关于疫苗的错误信息在社交媒体上大量涌现。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「普若利飞瑞特」——前半是「后代」，后半是「生出」：生出许多后代，就是激增

root: 逆构词：动词 proliferate 来自 1870 年代，由名词 proliferation 倒造；名词来自法语 prolifération（proliférer「产生后代」），最终由拉丁语 proles「后代」+ ferre「承担、生育」构成。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses progress from a quick growth in count, to biological reproduction, to spreading outward, to deliberate production of more, to diversification, to rising complexity, to sudden appearance of copies from a shared source, to wide dissemination of ideas.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从「数量迅速增长」出发，依次走向「生物性繁殖」、「向外扩散」、「有意识地制造更多」、「多样化增长」、「复杂度上升」、「有共同源头的副本突然大量出现」与「想法的广泛传播」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a petri dish where a few bacterial colonies have spread to fill almost the whole surface.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个培养皿里，几个细菌菌落已经扩散到几乎铺满整个表面。

branches.en: QUICK GROWTH IN COUNT: the most general sense, speed matters more than mechanism.
branches.cn: 数量的快速增长：最一般的义项，速度比机制更重要。

branches.en: BIOLOGICAL REPRODUCTION: the original literal sense of the word.
branches.cn: 生物繁殖：这个词最初的字面意思。

branches.en: SPREADING OUT AND DELIBERATE PRODUCTION: the same root applied to intentional human acts.
branches.cn: 向外扩散与有意识地制造：同样的词根用到了人的有意行为上。

branches.en: VARIETY AND COMPLEXITY: growth that is not just more but also different or harder to follow.
branches.cn: 多样化与复杂度：增长不只是更多，还变得不一样或更难跟进。

branches.en: SUDDEN COPIES AND IDEAS: a shared source or shared belief drives the reproduction.
branches.cn: 突然的副本与想法：一个共同源头或共同信念驱动了复制。

intro.en: Proliferate is a verb built on the noun proliferation, which is itself borrowed from French. The deep roots are Latin proles and ferre.
intro.cn: proliferate 是一个由名词 proliferation 倒造的动词，而后者又借自法语。最底层的拉丁词根是 proles 和 ferre。

latinIntro.en: Latin proles (offspring) and Latin ferre (to bear or carry) combine in French proliférer, which enters English through the noun proliferation.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 proles（后代）与 ferre（承担、生育）在法语里组合成 proliférer，它通过名词 proliferation 进入英语。

items.example: The verb we use, built in the 1870s.
items.exampleCN: 我们今天用的动词，1870 年代造的。

items.example: The noun that the verb is built from.
items.exampleCN: 动词就是从它来的。

items.example: The French source of the English noun.
items.exampleCN: 英语名词的法语来源。

items.example: The first Latin root.
items.exampleCN: 第一个拉丁词根。

items.example: The second Latin root, ancestor of ferry, transfer, refer.
items.exampleCN: 第二个拉丁词根，ferry、transfer、refer 都是它的后代。

items.example: An older adjective from the same family.
items.exampleCN: 同一家族里更老的形容词。

items.example: A direct borrowing of Latin proles via Old French progenie.
items.exampleCN: 经古法语 progenie 直接借自拉丁语 proles。

items.example: Turns French verbs into process nouns.
items.exampleCN: 把法语动词变成表示过程的名词。

derivatives.zh: 来自法语，义为「激增；大量繁殖」
proliferate 加 -ive 构成，义为「增殖性的」
来自同一家族，义为「多产的」
来自拉丁语 proles，义为「后代；后继者」

definition_zh: 刺激；激发；使活跃（使某物产生反应或使活动加速）
definition_en: to encourage or cause an activity, process or reaction to happen or to increase in intensity
core_image: 一根电极轻轻触碰蜗牛神经节，触手随即回缩；图像上用淡红色箭头标出刺激来源
scene: 实验室里，研究人员正寻找能让特定神经细胞作出反应的最低电流阈值。A mild electric current can stimulate certain nerve cells to fire repeatedly.
sceneCN: 这里取第 1 个义项（用外界因素引起生物体反应）；句意为温和的电流能刺激某些神经细胞反复放电。

pos.zh: 及物动词：刺激；激发；促使活动发生

derivatives.zh: 动词加 -tion 构成，义为「刺激；激发」
直接来自拉丁语 stimulus「刺棒」，义为「刺激物；激励」
来自同一拉丁词根，义为「兴奋剂；刺激物」
现在分词作形容词，义为「令人振奋的；有激励性的」

senses.title: To cause a biological reaction
senses.definition: to make an organism, cell or organ respond by applying a stimulus
senses.definitionCN: 通过施加刺激使生物体、细胞或器官作出反应
senses.example: Heat and cold both stimulate the skin's sensory receptors.
senses.exampleCN: 冷和热都能刺激皮肤上的感觉受体。
senses.why: The Latin root stimulus means a goad or spur — a pointed thing you poke with — so biological stimulation is literal poking.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 stimulus 意为「刺棒」——一种用来戳人的尖东西——所以生物刺激就是真的戳一下。

senses.title: To encourage an activity or process
senses.definition: to make a process begin or increase in pace
senses.definitionCN: 让一个过程开始或加快步伐
senses.example: Lower interest rates stimulate borrowing and spending.
senses.exampleCN: 降低利率能刺激借贷与消费。
senses.why: Here the goad is metaphorical; the economic process reacts to the poke the way a nerve does.
senses.whyCN: 这里刺棒是比喻用法；经济过程像神经那样对戳一下作出反应。

senses.title: To arouse interest or excitement
senses.definition: to make someone feel curious, enthusiastic or mentally active
senses.definitionCN: 让某人感到好奇、热情或精神活跃
senses.example: The documentary stimulated a lively discussion among the students.
senses.exampleCN: 这部纪录片在学生中激发了一场热烈讨论。
senses.why: Minds can be stimulated just as cells can be, and the word carries the root sense of waking something up.
senses.whyCN: 心智可以像细胞那样被刺激，这个词带着「把什么东西叫醒」的词根意思。

senses.title: To promote development or growth
senses.definition: to help something grow, develop or become stronger
senses.definitionCN: 帮助某物生长、发展或变得更强
senses.example: Regular fertilizer stimulates the growth of new leaves.
senses.exampleCN: 定期施肥能促进新叶生长。
senses.why: Growth needs more than a single poke, but the word can cover a sustained promoting effect too.
senses.whyCN: 生长不只是戳一下，但这个词也能覆盖持续的促进作用。

senses.title: To act as a stimulus for
senses.definition: to serve as the thing that makes another process happen
senses.definitionCN: 充当让另一个过程发生的那个东西
senses.example: The earthquake stimulated a wave of emergency building codes.
senses.exampleCN: 那次地震促使了一波紧急建筑法规出台。
senses.why: Some events are big enough to act as the stimulus themselves, not just respond to one.
senses.whyCN: 有些事件本身大到可以充当刺激物，而不只是对刺激作出反应。

senses.title: To increase energy or alertness
senses.definition: to make someone feel more energetic and awake
senses.definitionCN: 让某人感到更有精神、更清醒
senses.example: A strong cup of coffee stimulates her enough to finish the report.
senses.exampleCN: 一杯浓咖啡能让她足够精神，把报告写完。
senses.why: Stimulants work by poking the nervous system, a direct descendant of the original goad sense.
senses.whyCN: 兴奋剂的工作方式就是戳一下神经系统，这是最初那个「刺棒」意思的直接后代。

senses.title: To encourage thought or memory
senses.definition: to make a memory, idea or thought come to mind
senses.definitionCN: 让记忆、想法或念头浮现出来
senses.example: The scent of pine needles stimulated childhood memories of summer cabins.
senses.exampleCN: 松针的气味唤起了夏天小木屋的童年记忆。
senses.why: Sense stimuli don't only make bodies react; they also bring buried things to the surface of the mind.
senses.whyCN: 感官刺激不只让身体作出反应，也能把埋藏的东西拉到意识表层。

senses.title: To make something happen that was latent
senses.titleCN: 让潜伏的东西显现出来
senses.definition: to bring a potential or latent ability to active expression
senses.definitionCN: 让潜在或潜伏的能力主动表现出来
senses.example: The coach's belief stimulated abilities in the player that no one had noticed.
senses.exampleCN: 教练的相信激发了那个选手身上没人注意到的能力。
senses.why: Sometimes stimulation doesn't create something new; it just wakes up what was already there.
senses.whyCN: 有时候刺激不是创造新东西，只是把已经在那儿的叫醒。

intro.en: Stimulate comes from Latin stimulare, to prick or goad, built on stimulus, a goad or spur. English borrowed the verb in the sixteen-forties.
intro.cn: stimulate 来自拉丁语 stimulare「刺、用刺棒驱赶」，由 stimulus「刺棒、马刺」构成。英语在 1540 年代借入这个动词。

items.en: Stimulate entered English in the 1540s, first with the literal sense of goading or pricking.
items.cn: stimulate 于 1540 年代进入英语，最初字面意思是用刺棒驱赶或戳。

items.en: Stimulus meant a goad, spur or pointed stick used to urge an animal forward.
items.cn: 拉丁语 stimulus 指用来驱赶动物前进的刺棒、马刺或尖棒。

items.en: Stimulare was the verb to prick or goad, and later to incite or rouse.
items.cn: 拉丁语 stimulare 是动词，意为「刺、驱赶」，后来引申为「激励、唤起」。

items.en: After entering English the verb spread from literal goading to biological, economic, intellectual and emotional senses.
items.cn: 进入英语后，这个动词从字面的驱赶扩展到了生物、经济、智力与情感等领域。

items.era: THE SAME ROOT IN MODERN USE
items.en: Today the noun stimulus remains technical; the verb stimulate has become the everyday word for waking something up.
items.cn: 今天名词 stimulus 仍然偏技术，而动词 stimulate 已经变成叫醒某物的日常词。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin root stimulus; the second group lists verbs that encourage or cause activity.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁词根 stimulus；第二组是鼓励或引起活动的其他动词。

entries.definition: The thing that does the stimulating, from the Latin goad.
entries.definitionCN: 起刺激作用的那个东西，来自拉丁语的刺棒。

entries.definition: A substance that increases activity, still in the goad family.
entries.definitionCN: 能提高活动的物质，仍在「刺棒」家族里。

entries.definition: The act or result of stimulating.
entries.definitionCN: 刺激的行为或结果。

entries.definition: A native English word for the pointed object used on a horse.
entries.definitionCN: 英语本土词，指用来刺马的尖物。

entries.definition: Another word for a pointed stick used to drive animals, the same image as stimulus.
entries.definitionCN: 另一个指驱赶动物用的尖棒的词，和 stimulus 同属一个意象。

entries.definition: To give support or hope to someone, with a warmer tone than stimulate.
entries.definitionCN: 给某人支持或希望，语气比 stimulate 暖。

entries.definition: To cause a reaction, often a strong or negative one.
entries.definitionCN: 引起反应，常是强烈或负面的。

entries.definition: To cause an action, often by giving a specific cue.
entries.definitionCN: 促使行动，常通过给一个具体提示。

entries.definition: To wake up or bring out a feeling, less about speed and more about waking.
entries.definitionCN: 唤起感觉，不太强调速度，更强调从无到有。

entries.definition: To make something start, with a sharp quick sense like pulling a gun.
entries.definitionCN: 让某物开始，带有像扣扳机那样干脆快速的感觉。

normalIntro.en: The word comes from a Latin goad: a pointed stick used to poke animals into moving. Think of the word as poking something awake.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语的刺棒：一根用来戳动物让它们动起来的尖棍。把它想象成戳一下把什么东西戳醒。

normal.en: Visualise a shepherd with a goad — poke, and the animal moves.
normal.cn: 想象拿着刺棒的牧羊人——戳一下，动物就动起来。

normal.en: A mild electric current is just another kind of goad for nerves.
normal.cn: 温和的电流只是神经的另一种刺棒。

normal.en: Stimulus is the noun version of the same root; stimulate is the verb.
normal.cn: stimulus 是同一词根的名词形式，stimulate 是动词。

normal.en: The verb entered English in the 1540s with literal goad sense first.
normal.cn: 这个动词 1540 年代进入英语，最初只有字面的刺棒意思。

normal.en: Stimulants work by poking your nervous system, the same root meaning.
normal.cn: 兴奋剂通过戳你的神经系统起作用，还是那个词根意思。

abstract.en: Stimulation is any small event that wakes up a larger process.
abstract.cn: 刺激是任何能唤醒更大过程的小事件。

abstract.en: Minds and cells are both waiting to be poked into action.
abstract.cn: 心智和细胞都在等待被戳一下然后动起来。

abstract.en: The root meaning of a sharp point survives in every sense of the word.
abstract.cn: 一个尖点的词根意思，保存在这个词的每一个义项里。

examples.en: A good teacher knows how to stimulate curiosity without giving away the answer.
examples.cn: 好老师知道如何激发好奇心，同时不直接把答案说出来。

examples.en: The new policy stimulated investment from foreign companies.
examples.cn: 新政策刺激了外国公司的投资。

examples.en: Bright sunlight stimulates vitamin D production in the skin.
examples.cn: 明亮的阳光会刺激皮肤生成维生素 D。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「斯提缪雷特」——「斯提」是刺棒，「缪雷特」是动作：用刺棒戳一下让它动起来，就是刺激

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small pointed stick pokes a snail's antenna, which retracts immediately.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根小尖棍戳了一下蜗牛的触角，触角立刻缩回去。

branches.en: BIOLOGICAL REACTION: the most literal sense, closest to the original goad.
branches.cn: 生物性反应：最字面的义项，最接近最初的刺棒。

branches.en: PROCESSES AND EVENTS: the poke causes a process to speed up or an event to happen.
branches.cn: 过程与事件：戳一下让过程加速，或让事件发生。

branches.en: INTEREST AND EXCITEMENT: minds are poked awake, just like cells.
branches.cn: 兴趣与兴奋：心智被戳醒，和细胞一样。

branches.en: GROWTH AND DEVELOPMENT: a sustained promoting effect on something long-term.

branches.en: ENERGY, MEMORY, LATENT ABILITY: things inside the person that wake up when poked.
branches.cn: 精力、记忆、潜伏能力：人内部被戳醒的东西。

intro.en: Stimulate comes directly from the Latin verb stimulare, built on the noun stimulus. English adds no prefix to the root; only the verb-ending -ate shows its origin.

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries are stimulus (the goad) and stimulare (the verb to goad). Both still survive in English as stimulus and stimulate.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语词条是 stimulus（刺棒）和 stimulare（驱赶动词）。两者都保留在英语里，分别是 stimulus 和 stimulate。

definition_zh: 类似的；相似的；可比的（指在某些方面可对应，但不相同）
definition_en: comparable in certain respects, typically in a way that makes clearer the nature of the things compared
core_image: 两块形状和用途不同的拼图，边缘无法咬合，但都被蓝色半透明覆盖层圈住，表示它们在「蓝色」这一点上类似
scene: 科学家在解释新发现时常借助大家熟悉的日常现象。The flow of electricity in a wire is analogous to water moving through a pipe.
sceneCN: 这里取第 1 个义项（两个不同事物在某一方面具有可比较的对应关系）；句意为电线中的电流流动与水在管道中的流动是类似的。

pos.zh: 形容词：类似的；相似的；可比的

derivatives.zh: 来自同一希腊词根，义为「类似物；模拟的东西」
来自同一希腊词根，义为「类比；相似」

senses.title: Comparable in some specific respect
senses.titleCN: 在某一具体方面可比较
senses.definition: similar or corresponding in one particular way, without being identical
senses.definitionCN: 以某一种特定方式相似或对应，不必完全相同
senses.example: The human brain's pattern of folding is analogous to the wrinkling of dried fruit.
senses.exampleCN: 人脑的折叠形态与干水果的皱缩在某种方式上是类似的。
senses.why: The Greek root ana- means up to, logos means ratio; so analogous means up to the same ratio — similar in proportion.
senses.whyCN: 希腊词根 ana- 意为「到」，logos 意为「比例」；所以 analogous 就是「在比例上达到一致」——在比例上相似。

senses.title: Used to explain one thing by comparing to another
senses.definition: standing in for a clearer or simpler model that helps understanding
senses.definitionCN: 充当一个更清楚、更简单的模型，帮助理解
senses.example: Climate scientists use an analogy of a bathtub: heat coming in is analogous to the tap, heat leaving to the drain.
senses.exampleCN: 气候学家用浴缸作类比：进来的热量类似于水龙头，出去的热量类似于下水道。
senses.why: The reason we care about analogy is that one thing can light up the other — so analogous things are explanatory twins.
senses.whyCN: 我们在乎类比，是因为一件事能照亮另一件事——所以类似的东西就是互为解释的双胞胎。

senses.title: Functionally similar but not structurally identical
senses.definition: performing the same role or function in different systems
senses.definitionCN: 在不同系统里执行相同的角色或功能
senses.example: A bird's wing and an insect's wing are analogous: both enable flight, but they evolved separately.
senses.exampleCN: 鸟翅和昆虫翅是类似的：两者都能飞，但各自独立演化出来。
senses.why: In biology analogous structures are exactly this: same job, different origins — which the word captures perfectly.
senses.whyCN: 在生物学里，类似结构恰恰就是这个意思：同功能，不同起源——这个词完美抓住了这点。

senses.title: Abstractly similar in pattern
senses.definition: showing a shared structural pattern even when the substances are very different
senses.definitionCN: 展示出共同的结构模式，即使物质本身完全不同
senses.example: The branching pattern of a river is analogous to the shape of a neuron cell.
senses.exampleCN: 河流的分支形态与神经元细胞的形态在模式上类似。
senses.why: Pattern similarity is more abstract than functional similarity, and the word reaches up to this level too.
senses.whyCN: 模式相似比功能相似更抽象，这个词也能覆盖到这个层次。

senses.title: Corresponding in one domain to another
senses.titleCN: 在一个领域里对应另一个领域
senses.definition: matching between different fields of knowledge or between theory and experience
senses.definitionCN: 在不同知识领域之间或理论与经验之间相对应
senses.example: The rules of social networks are in some ways analogous to the laws of physical motion.
senses.exampleCN: 社交网络的规则在某些方面与物理运动定律类似。
senses.why: Cross-domain analogy is how science and philosophy often make progress.
senses.whyCN: 跨领域类比是科学与哲学常用来取得进展的方式。

senses.title: Similar in moral or legal standing
senses.titleCN: 在道德或法律地位上类似
senses.definition: having a comparable status or role in a rule-based system
senses.definitionCN: 在一个有规则的系统里具有可比较的地位或角色
senses.example: The digital document was treated as analogous to a signed paper contract.
senses.exampleCN: 这份数字文档被视为等同于签过字的纸质合同。
senses.why: In legal language analogous can mean 'treated as equivalent' for the sake of a rule.
senses.whyCN: 在法律语言里，analogous 可以指「为了适用某条规则而视为等同」。

senses.title: An analogy between two scientific theories
senses.titleCN: 两条科学理论之间的类比
senses.definition: standing in a comparable relation that helps scientists transfer ideas
senses.definitionCN: 处于一种可比较的关系中，帮助科学家迁移想法
senses.example: Quantum mechanics was built partly by reasoning by analogy with classical waves.
senses.exampleCN: 量子力学部分是通过与经典波动的类比推理建立起来的。
senses.why: Great theories often begin when one field sees something analogous in another.
senses.whyCN: 伟大的理论常常开始于一个领域在另一个领域里看到了类似的东西。

senses.title: Used with to for the explicit comparison
senses.titleCN: 与 to 搭配明确作比较
senses.definition: occurring in the pattern 'X is analogous to Y' where the comparison is pointed out directly
senses.definitionCN: 出现在「X is analogous to Y」的模式里，直接点明比较
senses.example: The English modal might is analogous to the French subjunctive tense in some uses.
senses.exampleCN: 英语里的 might 在某些用法上与法语的虚拟语气类似。
senses.why: The preposition to is required because the comparison needs something to anchor to.
senses.whyCN: 需要介词 to，是因为作比较必须有东西可以锚定。

intro.en: Analogous comes from Greek analogos meaning proportionate, built from ana- meaning up to or according to, and logos meaning ratio or account. Latin analogus borrowed the term, and English took it in the sixteen-forties.
intro.cn: analogous 来自希腊语 analogos「按比例的」，由 ana-「到、根据」与 logos「比例、说明」构成。拉丁语借为 analogus，英语于 1640 年代借入。

items.en: Analogous entered English in the sixteen-forties, first used in mathematical and logical writing.
items.cn: analogous 于 1640 年代进入英语，最初用于数学与逻辑写作。

items.en: The prefix ana- meant up to, according to or in proportion to.
items.cn: 希腊语前缀 ana- 意为「到、根据、成比例地」。

items.en: Logos meant ratio, word, reason or account, a central term in Greek philosophy.
items.cn: logos 意为「比例、话语、理由、说明」，是希腊哲学里的核心词。

items.en: Latin borrowed the Greek word as analogus, used of things corresponding in proportion.
items.cn: 拉丁语借为 analogus，指在比例上对应的东西。

items.en: After the seventeenth century the adjective spread from mathematics into biology, law, linguistics and general prose.
items.cn: 17 世纪之后，这个形容词从数学扩散到生物学、法律、语言学与一般散文中。

note.en: The first group shares the Greek root logos or the family of analogy; the second group lists adjectives of similarity with different shades.
note.cn: 第一组共享希腊词根 logos 或 analogy 家族；第二组是不同色彩的表示相似的形容词。

entries.definitionCN: 表示两个相似事物之间比较的名词。

entries.definition: A thing that is analogous to another; the British spelling of analog.
entries.definitionCN: 与另一事物类似的东西；analog 的英式拼法。

entries.definition: From logos meaning reason or account.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 logos「理由、说明」。

entries.definition: Two people speaking together, the -logue suffix from logos.
entries.definitionCN: 两人对话，后缀 -logue 来自 logos。

entries.definition: The study of life, the -logy suffix from logos.
entries.definitionCN: 研究生命的学科，后缀 -logy 来自 logos。

entries.definition: Having qualities in common, a much more general word than analogous.
entries.definitionCN: 有共同性质，比 analogous 宽泛得多。

entries.definition: Able to be compared, without implying actual similarity.
entries.definitionCN: 可被比较的，不暗示实际上相似。

entries.definition: Equal in value or function, stronger than analogous.
entries.definitionCN: 在价值或功能上相等，比 analogous 程度更高。

entries.definition: In biology, structures sharing a common origin — the opposite of analogous.
entries.definitionCN: 在生物学里，指有共同起源的结构——analogous 的反面。

entries.definition: Running side by side without meeting, often used abstractly of similar developments.
entries.definitionCN: 并行不相交，常抽象地用于类似发展。

normalIntro.en: Break it into ana- (up to, according to) and logos (ratio). So analogous means up to the same ratio — similar in proportion.
normalIntro.cn: 拆成 ana-（到、根据）和 logos（比例）。所以 analogous 就是「在比例上达到一致」。

normal.en: Elephant wings and bat wings are analogous — same job, different ancestors.
normal.cn: 象翅和蝙蝠翅是类似的——同功能，不同祖先。

normal.en: Electricity is analogous to water: current = flow, voltage = pressure.
normal.cn: 电类似水：电流 = 流量，电压 = 压力。

normal.en: Logos gives logic, dialogue, biology, analogy — a busy root.
normal.cn: logos 生出 logic、dialogue、biology、analogy——一个很忙的词根。

normal.en: Entered English in the 1640s via Latin analogus.
normal.cn: 通过拉丁语 analogus 于 1640 年代进入英语。

normal.en: Always followed by to when the comparison is explicit.
normal.cn: 当比较是明确的时候，总跟在 to 后面。

abstract.en: An analogy is a small door cut between two different rooms.
abstract.cn: 类比是在两个不同房间之间开的一扇小门。

abstract.en: Analogous things light up each other — otherwise nobody would care about the comparison.
abstract.cn: 类似的东西能互相照亮，否则没人在乎这个比较。

abstract.en: All human understanding leaks through analogies, whether we notice them or not.
abstract.cn: 人类所有的理解都在通过类比渗漏，不管我们有没有注意到。

examples.en: The way proteins fold is analogous to the way a string can coil into different shapes.
examples.cn: 蛋白质折叠的方式，与一根绳子能盘成不同形状类似。

examples.en: Military strategy is sometimes analogous to chess: the board is small, the rules are clear, but outcomes depend on imagination.
examples.cn: 军事战略有时类似于下棋：棋盘小，规则清楚，但结果取决于想象力。

examples.en: The growth of city suburbs is analogous to the expansion of a crystal.
examples.cn: 城市郊区的扩张类似于晶体的生长。

sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从「在某一具体方面可比较」出发，依次走向「充当解释模型」、「生物学里功能相同起源不同」、「抽象模式上相似」、「跨领域对应」、「法律或道德等同」、「跨领域科学类比」与显式的 X is analogous to Y 结构。

branches.en: THE BASIC COMPARISON: one thing matches another in some respect.
branches.cn: 基本比较：甲事在某方面对应乙事。

branches.en: EXPLANATION AND CROSS-DOMAIN USE: analogy makes the unfamiliar familiar.
branches.cn: 解释与跨领域用法：类比把陌生的东西变熟悉。

branches.en: FUNCTIONAL SIMILARITY WITH DIFFERENT ORIGINS: the biological sense of analogous structures.
branches.cn: 功能相同起源不同：生物学里类似结构的义项。

branches.en: PATTERN AND SCIENCE: analogy as a tool for building theories.
branches.cn: 模式与科学：类比作为构建理论的工具。

branches.en: RULES AND FORM: legal use of analogy, plus the required preposition pattern.
branches.cn: 规则与形式：法律中的类比用法，以及必须搭配介词的形式。

definition_zh: 连续的；连贯的；依次发生的（一个接一个不间断）
definition_en: following each other continuously without interruption
core_image: 一排亮着的交通信号灯，每个灯的熄灭紧接下一个亮起，中间没有空白间隔
scene: 考试周连考三天，学生们压力不小。After three consecutive nights without proper sleep, she could barely keep her eyes open in class.
sceneCN: 这里取第 1 个义项（多个事件一个接一个发生，没有中断）；句意为连续三个晚上没有好好睡觉之后，她上课几乎睁不开眼。
