senses.title: Following without interruption
senses.definition: coming one after another with no gaps or breaks
senses.definitionCN: 一个接一个地到来，中间没有空隙或间断
senses.example: The region suffered three consecutive years of drought.
senses.exampleCN: 该地区经历了连续三年的干旱。
senses.why: The Latin root sequi means to follow; consecutive describes things that follow each other without a gap.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 sequi 意为「跟随」；consecutive 描述的是东西之间没有空隙地互相跟随。

senses.title: In unbroken numerical or alphabetical order
senses.titleCN: 按无间断的数字或字母顺序
senses.definition: arranged in a sequence where each item is the next in a series
senses.definitionCN: 按每一项都是该系列中下一项的方式排列
senses.example: The room numbers on this floor are consecutive.
senses.exampleCN: 这一层楼的房间号是连续的。
senses.why: Numbers that follow without skipping are the cleanest example of the root meaning.
senses.whyCN: 不跳着的连续数字是这个词根意思最干净的例子。

senses.title: Back-to-back with no pause
senses.definition: happening one after another in quick succession, with no pause between them
senses.definitionCN: 紧接着发生，中间没有停顿
senses.example: She had three consecutive meetings before lunch.
senses.exampleCN: 午饭前她有三个连着的会议。
senses.why: The word emphasizes the lack of interruption more than it emphasizes the speed.
senses.whyCN: 这个词更强调「没有中断」，而不是速度有多快。

senses.title: Following logically from the previous
senses.titleCN: 在逻辑上跟上一个相关
senses.definition: standing as the necessary or expected result of what came before
senses.definitionCN: 作为前面那件事的必然或预期结果而出现
senses.example: The consecutive chapters each build on the theory set out in the first.
senses.exampleCN: 后面的章节依次建立在第一章提出的理论之上。
senses.why: Logical consecution is a less concrete sense, where one idea naturally follows the next.
senses.whyCN: 逻辑上的连续是一个更抽象的义项，指一个想法自然地跟着下一个。

senses.title: Consecutive sentence in grammar
senses.definition: a grammatical term for a clause or phrase that follows as the natural consequence of the main clause
senses.definitionCN: 语法术语，指作为主句自然结果而跟进的从句或短语
senses.example: The consecutive clause explains what happens once the condition is met.
senses.exampleCN: 连续从句解释了一旦条件满足会发生什么。
senses.why: This technical sense from rhetoric survives in grammar textbooks.
senses.whyCN: 这个来自修辞学的技术义项保留在语法教科书里。

senses.title: Consecutive interpreting or translation
senses.definition: a mode of interpreting where the speaker pauses and the interpreter speaks after each chunk
senses.definitionCN: 一种口译方式：讲者每说完一段停下来，译员跟上翻译
senses.example: She works best in consecutive mode rather than simultaneous.
senses.exampleCN: 她在连续口译模式下比同传做得更好。
senses.why: Here consecutive means the interpreter follows the speaker, not overlapping with them.
senses.whyCN: 这里 consecutive 指译员跟随讲者，而不是与讲者同时进行。

senses.title: Lying along the same line
senses.definition: placed end to end in a straight line or chain
senses.definitionCN: 头尾相接排成一条直线或链条
senses.example: The house has five consecutive rooms along its main corridor.
senses.exampleCN: 这栋房子主走廊两旁有五间相连的房间。
senses.why: Spatial consecution is another concrete use of the same follow-each-other image.
senses.whyCN: 空间上的连续是同一个「互相跟随」意象的又一个具体用法。

senses.title: Marked by continuation rather than new beginnings
senses.titleCN: 以延续而非新开端为特征
senses.definition: describing a pattern that keeps going from where it left off, rather than starting fresh each time
senses.definitionCN: 描述一种从上次停下的地方继续、而不是每次重新开始的模式
senses.example: The team's consecutive record over the last decade is unmatched.
senses.exampleCN: 该队过去十年的连续战绩无人能及。
senses.why: This sense is common in sports, where consecutive games or wins build a streak.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项常见于体育，连续的比赛或胜场构成一个 streak。

intro.en: Consecutive comes from French consécutif, borrowed from Latin consecutivus meaning following closely, built on the past participle of consequi, to follow closely. The Latin root sequi means to follow.
intro.cn: consecutive 来自法语 consécutif，借自拉丁语 consecutivus「紧随其后的」，后者由 consequi「紧紧跟随」的过去分词构成。拉丁词根 sequi 意为「跟随」。

items.en: Consecutive entered English in the sixteen-tens, borrowed from French.
items.cn: consecutive 于 1610 年代借入英语，借自法语。

items.en: Consequi meant to follow closely, from con- with + sequi to follow.
items.cn: consequi 意为「紧紧跟随」，由 con-「一起」+ sequi「跟随」构成。

items.en: Consecutivus was the adjective built on the past participle consectus of consequi.
items.cn: consecutivus 是由 consequi 的过去分词 consectus 构成的形容词。

items.en: French adopted the Latin adjective as consécutif, which English then borrowed.
items.cn: 法语把这个拉丁形容词借为 consécutif，英语再借入。

items.en: The root sequi gives English sequence, sequel, consequence, execute, obsequious and many more.
items.cn: 词根 sequi 生出英语的 sequence、sequel、consequence、execute、obsequious 等众多词。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin root sequi 'to follow'; the second group lists other words for uninterrupted succession.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁词根 sequi「跟随」；第二组是表示不间断连续的其他词。

entries.definition: A related noun meaning an ordered succession of things.
entries.definitionCN: 来自同一词根的名词，指有序的连续。

entries.definition: A work that follows another, literally 'the one that follows'.
entries.definitionCN: 跟随另一部作品而来的东西，字面就是「跟随者」。

entries.definition: A result that follows from an action.
entries.definitionCN: 跟随某一行动而来的结果。

entries.definition: From ex- + sequi, to follow through completely.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 ex- + sequi，意为「彻底地跟进完成」。

entries.definition: Ready to follow and obey, from the same root.
entries.definitionCN: 乐于跟随服从的，来自同一词根。

entries.definition: Following in order, very close in meaning to consecutive.
entries.definitionCN: 按顺序跟随，与 consecutive 意思非常近。

entries.definition: Continuing without a break, more about duration than about ordered sequence.
entries.definitionCN: 持续不断，更强调时长而非有序顺序。

entries.definition: Arranged in a series, often published in parts.
entries.definitionCN: 排成系列，常分部分出版。

entries.definition: A consecutive count kept over time, as in 'a running total'.
entries.definitionCN: 随时间持续累积的连续计数，如 running total。

entries.definition: Not interrupted, focusing on the lack of breaks rather than ordered sequence.
entries.definitionCN: 未被打断的，强调没有缺口而非有序序列。

normalIntro.en: Think of consecutive as things that follow each other, from Latin sequi to follow. No gaps, no skips.
normalIntro.cn: 把 consecutive 想象成互相跟随的东西，来自拉丁语 sequi「跟随」。没有缺口，没有跳过。

normal.en: Consecutive numbers: 1, 2, 3, 4 — no skips, each follows the last.
normal.cn: 连续数字：1、2、3、4——不跳，每个跟着上一个。

normal.en: Win six consecutive games = win six games in a row, no losses in between.
normal.cn: 连胜六场 = 连续赢六场，中间没有输。

normal.en: The sequi family gives sequence, sequel, consequence, execute — all about following.
normal.cn: sequi 家族生出 sequence、sequel、consequence、execute——全都和「跟随」有关。

normal.en: Entered English in the 1610s via French consécutif.
normal.cn: 通过法语 consécutif 于 1610 年代借入英语。

normal.en: Interpreters work in consecutive or simultaneous mode — two ways of following the speaker.
normal.cn: 译员要么用连续模式要么用同传模式——两种跟随讲者的方式。

abstract.en: Consecutive is time without breathing room.
abstract.cn: consecutive 是没有呼吸间隙的时间。

abstract.en: Every streak, every dynasty, every musical phrase is a little chain of consecutive items.
abstract.cn: 每一个连胜、每一个王朝、每一段乐句，都是一串连续的东西。

abstract.en: The opposite of consecutive is not just separate; it is skipped.
abstract.cn: consecutive 的反面不只是分开，更是被跳过。

examples.en: The team won eight consecutive games before losing its first match of the season.
examples.cn: 该队在输掉本赛季第一场比赛之前，已经连胜八场。

examples.en: She has spent eighteen consecutive summers working as a park ranger in Alaska.
examples.cn: 她已经连续十八个夏天在阿拉斯加当公园管理员。

examples.en: The document contains five consecutive chapters describing the same experiment.
examples.cn: 这份文件包含五章连续描写同一个实验的内容。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「康塞奎提夫」——「康」连着，「塞奎」跟着，「提夫」是形容词：连着跟着，就是连续

root: 拉丁语 consequi（con-「一起」+ sequi「跟随」）→ consecutivus（过去分词 consectus 构成的形容词）→ 法语 consécutif → 英语 consecutive（1610 年代）；同词根 family 包括 sequence、sequel、consequence、execute、obsequious 等。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from following without interruption, to numerical sequence, to back-to-back events, to logical consequence, to the grammatical consecutive clause, to the consecutive interpreting mode, to spatial adjacency in a line, to a pattern of continued success.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从「不间断地紧随其后」出发，依次走向「数字或字母顺序连续」、「一个接一个没有停顿」、「逻辑上的必然结果」、「语法上的连续从句」、「连续口译模式」、「空间上排成一条直线」与「持续成功的模式」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a row of traffic lights where each one lights up the moment the previous one goes out.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排交通信号灯，每个亮起的瞬间就是上一个熄灭的瞬间。

branches.en: THE BASIC UNBROKEN SEQUENCE: the root meaning of the word.
branches.cn: 基本的无间断序列：这个词的根本意思。

branches.en: NUMERICAL OR ALPHABETICAL ORDER: the clearest example of consecutive items.
branches.cn: 数字或字母顺序：连续东西最清楚的例子。

branches.en: BACK-TO-BACK EVENTS AND LOGICAL CONSECUENCE: the same structure applied to meetings and ideas.
branches.cn: 接连的事件与逻辑结果：同一个结构用到了会议和想法上。

branches.en: LOGICAL AND GRAMMATICAL CONSEQUENCE: the same root in the more technical domains.
branches.cn: 逻辑与语法上的结果：同一个词根用到更技术的领域里。

branches.en: INTERPRETING, SPACING AND PERFORMANCE: the word travels into work practices, architecture and sports.
branches.cn: 口译、空间排列与体育表现：这个词走进了职业操作、建筑与体育。

intro.en: Consecutive is built on Latin consequi, from con- and sequi. French reshaped the Latin adjective, and English borrowed the French form.
intro.cn: consecutive 由拉丁语 consequi 构成，后者来自 con- 与 sequi。法语改造了这个拉丁形容词，英语借入法语形式。

latinIntro.en: Latin sequi is a root meaning to follow, appearing in many common English words. The compound consequi adds con- for 'together'.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根 sequi 意为「跟随」，出现在许多常见英语词里。复合词 consequi 加上了 con-「一起」。

items.example: The English adjective.
items.exampleCN: 英语形容词本身。

items.example: The direct Latin source of the French form.
items.exampleCN: 法语形式的直接拉丁来源。

items.example: Built from con- + sequi.
items.exampleCN: 由 con- + sequi 构成。

items.example: Adds the sense of being together in the following.
items.exampleCN: 给「跟随」加上一起的感觉。

items.example: The foundational root, ancestor of sequence, sequel, consequence.
items.exampleCN: 基础词根，sequence、sequel、consequence 的祖先。

items.example: A common noun from the same root.
items.exampleCN: 同一词根的常见名词。

items.example: Literally 'the one that follows'.
items.exampleCN: 字面就是「跟随者」。

items.example: A result that follows from an action.
items.exampleCN: 跟随行动而来的结果。

items.example: Completely following through on a plan.
items.exampleCN: 彻底跟进一个计划。

derivatives.zh: consecutive 加 -ly 构成
来自同一拉丁词根，义为「连续；连贯」
来自 sequi，义为「序列；顺序」
来自同一词根，义为「顺序的」

definition_zh: 离散的；分离的；独立的；不连续的（与 continuous 相对）
definition_en: consisting of distinct, separate items or parts; not continuous or flowing together
core_image: 棋盘上的黑白棋子，每个棋子都是独立可移动的个体，彼此之间有明显间隔
scene: 数据结构课上老师在讲两种变量类型。Unlike continuous height measurements, number of children is a discrete variable with only whole-number values.
sceneCN: 这里取第 1 个义项（数据只能取离散值、不能连续变化）；句意为身高的测量值是连续的，而孩子的数量是只能取整数值的离散变量。

pos.zh: 形容词：离散的；分离的；独立的

derivatives.zh: 形容词加 -ly 构成，义为「离散地；独立地」
形容词加 -ness 构成，义为「离散性」
同词根拼法相同、语义分离的另一个词，义为「谨慎的；审慎的」
来自同一拉丁词根 cernere「分离、决定」，义为「辨别；看出」

senses.title: Data or variables with distinct separate values
senses.titleCN: 取值离散的数据或变量
senses.definition: taking only specific separated values, as opposed to values that can fall anywhere on a range
senses.definitionCN: 只能取特定的、互相分开的值，而不是在一个范围里任何位置都可以
senses.example: Number of cars sold per day is discrete, because it can only be a whole number.
senses.exampleCN: 每天卖出的汽车数量是离散的，因为它只能是整数。
senses.why: The Latin root cernere means to separate or decide; discrete names things that have been separated into distinct units.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 cernere 意为「分离、决定」；discrete 指的是被分离成独立单元的东西。

senses.title: Made up of separate individual parts
senses.titleCN: 由独立的个体部件构成
senses.definition: having parts that are separate from each other and not connected smoothly
senses.definitionCN: 各部分互相分开，没有平滑连接
senses.example: The city's subway system is built from several discrete lines that only meet at a few hubs.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市的地铁系统由几条独立的线路构成，只在少数几个枢纽站汇合。
senses.why: Physical discreteness is easy to picture — Lego blocks are discrete, a sheet of paper is not.
senses.whyCN: 物理上的离散很容易想象：乐高积木是离散的，一张纸不是。

senses.title: Separate and self-contained
senses.definition: existing as an independent unit with its own boundaries
senses.definitionCN: 以有自己边界的独立单元存在
senses.example: Each chapter of the book is a discrete unit that can be read on its own.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书的每一章都是可以独立阅读的单元。
senses.why: Ideas and chapters can be discrete too, when they have separate boundaries.
senses.whyCN: 想法和章节也可以是离散的，只要它们有各自的边界。

senses.title: Not continuous in time
senses.definition: occurring in separate episodes rather than flowing into one another
senses.definitionCN: 以独立片段出现，而不是流在一起
senses.example: The pain came in discrete waves, with quiet gaps between them.
senses.exampleCN: 疼痛以一阵一阵独立的波次出现，中间有安静的空隙。
senses.why: Time itself flows, but events in time can be discrete.
senses.whyCN: 时间本身在流动，但时间里的事件可以是离散的。

senses.title: Mathematics: separate as opposed to continuous
senses.titleCN: 数学上离散（与连续相对）
senses.definition: a technical term for structures where each element has neighbors but no element flows into the next
senses.definitionCN: 数学技术术语，指每个元素有邻居但不会流入下一个的结构
senses.example: Graphs are discrete structures; the real number line is a continuous one.
senses.exampleCN: 图是离散结构，实数轴是连续结构。
senses.why: Mathematics gives the word its cleanest technical meaning.
senses.whyCN: 数学给了这个词最干净的技术义项。

senses.title: Philosophy: separate as distinct from indistinguishable
senses.definition: standing out as a distinct thing, not merging into its surroundings
senses.definitionCN: 作为一个独特的东西凸显出来，不融入周围环境
senses.example: The argument treats consciousness as a discrete property of the brain.
senses.exampleCN: 这个论证把意识当作大脑的一个独立属性。
senses.why: Philosophers use discrete when they want to stress that a property is not reducible to its parts.
senses.whyCN: 哲学家在用 discrete 时，是想强调某一属性不能还原为它的组成部分。

senses.title: Discrete vs. discreet: two spellings, two senses from one root
senses.definition: note that the spelling discrete means separate, while discreet means careful; both descend from Latin discernere
senses.definitionCN: 注意拼写 discrete 指分离，而 discreet 指谨慎；两者都来自拉丁语 discernere
senses.example: She was discrete about her research results but discreet about her sources.
senses.exampleCN: 她把研究结果整理成独立单元呈现，但对数据来源保持谨慎。
senses.why: This is an important usage note: discrete and discreet are not the same word, even though they share a root.
senses.whyCN: 这是一个重要用法提示：discrete 和 discreet 不是同一个词，尽管它们同根。

senses.title: Standing alone as a category
senses.definition: belonging to a category that is distinct from nearby or related categories
senses.definitionCN: 属于一个与邻近或相关类别明显不同的类别
senses.example: This species forms a discrete branch of the evolutionary tree.
senses.exampleCN: 这个物种在进化树上形成一个独立的分支。
senses.why: Taxonomies depend on discreteness — each category must be distinguishable from its neighbours.
senses.whyCN: 分类依赖离散性——每个类别都必须能与邻居区分开来。

intro.en: Discrete and discreet descend from the same Latin root, discernere, to separate, distinguish. Latin discretus meant separate, distinct, and also, by extension, prudent. The two senses diverged after entering English.
intro.cn: discrete 与 discreet 都来自同一拉丁词根 discernere「分离、辨别」。拉丁语 discretus 既指「分离的、不同的」，后来引申为「审慎的」。两个义项在进入英语后分叉。

items.en: Discrete entered English in the fifteen-seventies with the sense separate, distinct.
items.cn: discrete 于 1570 年代进入英语，义为「分离的、不同的」。

items.en: Discernere meant to separate, distinguish or decide, from dis- apart + cernere to separate.
items.cn: discernere 意为「分离、辨别、决定」，来自 dis-「分开」+ cernere「分离」。

items.en: Discretus was the past participle of discernere, meaning separated or distinct.
items.cn: discretus 是 discernere 的过去分词，意为「分离的、不同的」。

items.en: Latin discretus also developed the extended sense careful or prudent, which English borrowed as discreet.
items.cn: 拉丁语 discretus 还发展出「小心、审慎」的引申义，英语借为 discreet。

items.en: Today discrete means separate and discreet means careful; the two spellings keep the old semantic split.
items.cn: 今天 discrete 指分离，discreet 指谨慎；两种拼写维持了古老的语义分裂。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin root cernere; the second group lists words that mean separate or unconnected.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁词根 cernere；第二组是表示分离或不相连的其他词。

entries.definition: Careful or prudent, from the same Latin participle — a different word in modern English.
entries.definitionCN: 谨慎的、审慎的，来自同一拉丁分词——现代英语里是一个不同的词。

entries.definition: To recognize or distinguish, the verb built directly from discernere.
entries.definitionCN: 识别、辨别，直接由 discernere 构成的动词。

entries.definition: To distinguish unfairly or justly, from the same root.
entries.definitionCN: 辨别（公正或不公正地），来自同一词根。

entries.definition: From con- + cernere, to sift together, hence to involve oneself with.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 con- + cernere「一起筛选」，引申为「关心、涉及」。

entries.definition: A decision or order, built from the same cernere 'decide' sense.
entries.definitionCN: 裁决、命令，来自 cernere「决定」之义。

entries.definition: A more everyday word for things that are not joined together.
entries.definitionCN: 更日常的词，指不连在一起的东西。

entries.definition: Clearly different or separate, very close to discrete in formal use.
entries.definitionCN: 明显不同或分开的，在正式用法里与 discrete 很接近。

entries.definition: Having breaks or interruptions, especially in time or space.
entries.definitionCN: 有断点的，尤其是在时间或空间上。

entries.definition: One thing considered separately from others of the same kind.
entries.definitionCN: 从同类中单独拿出来看的一件事。

entries.definition: Limited or countable, related to discrete in mathematics.
entries.definitionCN: 有限的、可数的，在数学上与 discrete 相关。

normalIntro.en: Discrete means separated out into distinct pieces, from Latin discernere to separate. Think of the opposite of continuous.
normalIntro.cn: discrete 意为分离成独立的小块，来自拉丁语 discernere「分离」。想成 continuous（连续的）的反面。

normal.en: Discrete data = integer counts; continuous data = anything in between.
normal.cn: 离散数据 = 整数计数；连续数据 = 任何中间值都可以。

normal.en: Lego blocks are discrete; a stretch of road is continuous.
normal.cn: 乐高积木是离散的；一段路是连续的。

normal.en: Discrete ≠ discreet: one means separate, the other means careful.
normal.cn: discrete ≠ discreet：前者指分离，后者指谨慎。

normal.en: Both come from Latin discretus, from discerere to separate.
normal.cn: 两者都来自拉丁语 discretus，来自 discernere「分离」。

normal.en: Entered English in the 1570s.
normal.cn: 1570 年代进入英语。

abstract.en: Discreteness is what allows the world to be counted.
abstract.cn: 离散性让世界可以被计数。

abstract.en: Every category is built on discreteness — if two things can't be told apart, there is no category.
abstract.cn: 每个类别都建立在离散性之上——如果两样东西分不出来，就没有类别。

abstract.en: The flip side of discrete is not just continuous; it is 'blurred together'.
abstract.cn: discrete 的反面不只是连续，更是「混在一起」。

examples.en: The researchers treated each interview as a discrete source of evidence rather than combining them.
examples.cn: 研究人员把每一次访谈都当作独立的证据来源，而不是把它们合并起来。

examples.en: Quantum theory suggests that energy comes in discrete packets called quanta.
examples.cn: 量子理论表明，能量以名为量子的离散包的形式出现。

examples.en: The region is divided into four discrete ecological zones with little species overlap.
examples.cn: 该地区被分成四个独立的生态区，物种几乎没有重叠。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「迪斯克里特」——「迪斯」分开，「克里特」筛出去：一个一个分离开，就是离散

root: 拉丁语 discernere（dis-「分开」+ cernere「分离、决定」）→ discretus「分离的；审慎的」→ 进入英语后分叉：discrete 保留下游「分离」义（1570 年代），discreet 保留「审慎」义；同词根 family 包括 discern、discriminate、concern、decree 等。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from discrete data or variables, to discrete physical parts, to discrete independent units, to events separated in time, to the mathematical opposition to continuous, to the philosophical idea of distinct properties, to the important spelling distinction with discreet, to discrete branches in taxonomies.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从「离散数据或变量」出发，依次走向「离散的物理部件」、「独立自足的单元」、「时间上不连续的事件」、「数学上与连续相对」、「哲学上的独立属性」、「与 discreet 的重要拼写区分」以及「分类中的独立分支」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: chess pieces standing separately on a board, each a distinct unit with clear boundaries.
core.cn: 核心意象：棋盘上分立的棋子，每个都是边界清晰的独立单元。

branches.en: DATA AND VARIABLES: the technical starting point in science and statistics.
branches.cn: 数据与变量：科学和统计里的技术起点。

branches.en: PHYSICAL AND CONCEPTUAL PARTS: the same idea applied to buildings and chapters.
branches.cn: 物理与概念部件：同一个想法用到了楼房和章节上。

branches.en: TIME AS DISCRETE: events separated by gaps rather than flowing.
branches.cn: 时间上的离散：被空隙分开而不是流在一起的事件。

branches.en: MATHEMATICS AND PHILOSOPHY: the technical home of the word.

definition_en: to explain the cause or reason for something; to constitute a specified proportion of something

scene: 年度报告里需要解释每一项开支的去向。Electric vehicles now account for nearly twenty percent of new car sales in China.

senses.title: To explain why something happens
senses.definition: to provide a reason or explanation for a fact, event or situation
senses.definitionCN: 为一个事实、事件或情境提供原因或解释
senses.example: Scientists cannot account for the sudden rise in frog populations in this pond.
senses.exampleCN: 科学家无法解释这个池塘里青蛙数量为何突然增加。
senses.why: The noun account meant a reckoning; to account for something is to give the reckoning that explains it.
senses.whyCN: 名词 account 本来指账目；account for 就是把能解释某事的那笔账算清楚。

senses.title: To make up a proportion or percentage
senses.titleCN: 构成某个比例或百分比
senses.definition: to constitute a specified fraction or percentage of a larger whole
senses.definitionCN: 构成一个更大整体中的某个特定分数或百分比
senses.example: Immigrant workers account for nearly one third of the region's construction labour.
senses.exampleCN: 外来务工人员占该地区建筑劳动力的近三分之一。
senses.why: This is a counting sense: you add up the pieces and the thing you're counting reaches a certain share.
senses.whyCN: 这是一个计数义项：你把碎片加起来，数到的东西就占了某个份额。

senses.title: To take responsibility for or handle
senses.definition: to be responsible for dealing with something or someone
senses.definitionCN: 负责处理某事或某人
senses.example: Someone has to account for the missing inventory before we ship the next batch.
senses.exampleCN: 在我们发下一批货之前，必须有人对丢失的库存负责。
senses.why: If you gave out something, you must be able to account for where it went.
senses.whyCN: 如果你发放了什么东西，你就必须能交代它去了哪里。

senses.title: To kill or destroy (informal, usually passive)
senses.titleCN: 消灭、干掉（口语，常用于被动）
senses.definition: to kill, destroy or disable something or someone
senses.definitionCN: 杀死、摧毁或致残某物或某人
senses.example: Half the enemy squadron was accounted for before they reached the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 敌方战机中队在抵达海岸之前，就被消灭了一半。
senses.why: This older military sense survives in the passive; the idea is to reckon someone as 'paid for' the damage they caused.
senses.whyCN: 这个较旧的军事义项保留在被动形式里；意思是把某人当作已经为自己造成的损失「偿清」了。

senses.title: To consider or judge (archaic)
senses.definition: to hold an opinion or form a judgement about something
senses.definitionCN: 对某事持有观点或形成判断
senses.example: She accounted the opportunity as a gift rather than a burden.
senses.exampleCN: 她把这个机会视为礼物而非负担。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense, now mostly archaic, coming directly from the Latin putare 'to think, reckon'.
senses.whyCN: 这是最老的义项，如今大多已经古旧，直接来自拉丁语 putare「认为、计算」。

senses.title: To give a formal accounting of
senses.definition: to provide a formal statement or report about something one is responsible for
senses.definitionCN: 对自己负责的事提供一份正式陈述或报告
senses.example: The manager must account for every dollar spent from the department budget.
senses.exampleCN: 经理必须对部门预算里花出去的每一美元都作出交代。
senses.why: This is a specialized sense used in auditing, public finance and governance.
senses.whyCN: 这是审计、公共财政和治理中的一个专门义项。

senses.title: To make allowance for or consider
senses.definition: to take something into consideration before making a judgement
senses.definitionCN: 在作出判断之前把某事考虑进去
senses.example: The exam accounts for the fact that students study in very different conditions.
senses.exampleCN: 这份考试考虑到了学生学习条件差异很大这一事实。
senses.why: Here account for means 'to keep in the reckoning' rather than 'to explain' or 'to kill'.
senses.whyCN: 这里 account for 的意思是「把……留在账里」，而不是「解释」或「干掉」。

senses.title: To explain away or dismiss
senses.definition: to provide an explanation that removes the need for further concern
senses.definitionCN: 提供一个解释，让事情不再需要担忧
senses.example: He tried to account for his absence by saying his train had been cancelled.
senses.exampleCN: 他试图用火车被取消来解释自己的缺席。
senses.why: This sense comes close to making excuses, though it can be neutral.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项接近找借口，但也可以是中性的。

intro.en: Account comes from Latin computare, to sum up or reckon together, through Old French acompte. The phrasal verb account for grew within English from the older noun sense of a reckoning.
intro.cn: account 来自拉丁语 computare「合计、计算」，经古法语 acompte 传入。短语动词 account for 是在英语内部由名词「账目」之义长出来的。

items.en: Account first appeared as a noun in Middle English around 1300, meaning a reckoning or calculation.
items.cn: account 于 1300 年前后首次作为中古英语名词出现，义为「计算、账目」。

items.en: From com- together + putare to reckon, think, or value.
items.cn: 由 com-「一起」+ putare「计算、认为、估价」构成。

items.en: French reshaped the Latin past participle computatus into acompte, a bill or reckoning.
items.cn: 法语把拉丁语过去分词 computatus 改造成 acompte，意为账单或计算。

items.en: The noun began to be used as a verb by the sixteenth century; the phrasal verb account for formed later.
items.cn: 名词在十六世纪开始被用作动词；短语动词 account for 之后才形成。

items.en: From reckoning and calculation the phrase spread to explaining, to counting proportions, to responsibility, and even to military killing.
items.cn: 从计算和账目的意思，这个短语扩展到解释、占比例、负责，甚至军事上的消灭。

note.en: The first group shares the root account or the Latin computare; the second group lists phrases that mean to explain or to constitute a proportion.
note.cn: 第一组共享 account 或拉丁语 computare 词根；第二组是表示解释或构成比例的其他短语。

entries.definitionCN: 另一个短语动词，意为「有分量、有意义」。

entries.definitionCN: 形式化的计算行为，来自 computare。

entries.definitionCN: 两笔账或两次计算之间的不匹配，来自同一计算家族。

entries.definition: Supposed or assumed, from putare 'to think'.
entries.definitionCN: 假定的、被认为的，来自 putare「认为」。

entries.definition: To make something clear by giving details, more general than account for.
entries.definitionCN: 通过给出细节让某事清楚，比 account for 更宽泛。

entries.definition: To constitute a proportion, similar to the percentage sense of account for.
entries.definitionCN: 构成某个比例，与 account for 的百分比义项相似。

entries.definition: To be responsible for dealing with something, like the responsibility sense.
entries.definitionCN: 负责处理某事，与 account for 的负责义项相似。

entries.definition: To take something into account or to be forced to face its consequences.
entries.definitionCN: 考虑到某事，或被迫面对其后果。

entries.definition: To take responsibility for something, very close to the responsibility sense of account for.
entries.definitionCN: 为某事负责，与 account for 的负责义项非常接近。

normalIntro.en: Account for grows from account = a reckoning or bill. To account for something is to present the reckoning that explains it.

normal.en: Think of a company accountant: they have to account for every dollar.
normal.cn: 想象一个公司会计：他们必须交代每一美元的去向。

normal.cn: 词根来自拉丁语 computare「合计计算」——和 compute 同根。

normal.cn: 例句：电动车占销量的 20%——这是比例义项。

normal.cn: account for = 解释，占比例，消灭——三种不同工作。

normal.cn: 1300 年前后作为名词进入英语；短语动词后来才形成。

abstract.en: Accounting for the world is the oldest intellectual habit.
abstract.cn: 为世界作出解释是最古老的智识习惯。

abstract.en: Every percentage figure on a pie chart is an act of accounting.
abstract.cn: 饼图上的每一个百分比数字，都是一次计数行为。

examples.cn: 可再生能源如今占这个国家电力的百分之四十以上。

examples.en: The teacher could not account for why half the class arrived an hour late.
examples.cn: 老师无法解释为什么半个班都迟到了一个小时。

examples.en: Three aircraft from the squadron were never accounted for after the battle.
examples.cn: 该中队有三架飞机在战斗之后再也没有下落。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from explaining why something happens, to constituting a proportion or percentage, to being responsible for handling, to killing in warfare, to the older archaic sense of thinking or judging, to formal auditing, to taking into account, and to explaining away.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从「解释某事发生的原因」出发，依次走向「构成某个比例或百分比」、「负责处理」、「军事上消灭」、「古旧的认为/判断」、「正式审计交代」、「考虑顾及」与「解释掉/找借口」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ledger with two columns — one gives the explanation, the other the proportion.
core.cn: 核心意象：一本有两栏的账本——一栏给解释，一栏给比例。

branches.en: EXPLANATION: the core intellectual use of the phrase.
branches.cn: 解释：这个短语最核心的智识用法。

branches.en: PROPORTION: the counting sense, where pieces are added up to a percentage.
branches.cn: 比例：计数义项，碎片加起来得到一个百分比。

branches.en: RESPONSIBILITY FORMAL AND CASUAL: handling something, either in daily work or in formal audit.
branches.cn: 负责——正式与日常：处理某事，无论是日常工作还是正式审计。

branches.en: MILITARY KILLING: the grim sense of settling accounts with enemies.
branches.cn: 军事上消灭：与敌人结清那笔账的残酷义项。

branches.en: THINKING, CONSIDERING, MAKING EXCUSES: older and softer senses still active.
branches.cn: 思考、考虑、找借口：更老也更温和的义项仍然活跃。

senses.title: To change oneself to fit a new situation
senses.titleCN: 改变自身以适应新情况
senses.definition: to modify one's behaviour, mindset or habits to suit changed circumstances
senses.definitionCN: 改变自己的行为、心态或习惯以适应变化的情况
senses.example: It takes most people several months to adapt to living in a foreign country.
senses.exampleCN: 大多数人都需要几个月才能适应在外国生活。
senses.why: The Latin root aptus means fit or suited; adapt means to move toward being fit, ad- toward + aptus fit.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 aptus 意为「适合的」；adapt 就是朝「适合」的方向走——ad-「向」+ aptus「适合」。

senses.title: To change something so it works in a new context
senses.titleCN: 改变某物使其在新语境下能用
senses.definition: to modify a tool, system or plan so it functions in a different setting
senses.definitionCN: 修改一个工具、系统或计划，使其能在不同环境下运作
senses.example: Engineers adapted the ship's radar to work on aircraft.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师把舰船上的雷达改装到飞机上使用。
senses.why: The verb can be used transitively too — you adapt a tool to a new purpose.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词也可以作及物——你把一个工具改装成新用途。

senses.title: Biology: to develop traits that improve survival
senses.titleCN: 生物学上发展出提升生存的特征
senses.definition: to evolve traits that make an organism better suited to its environment
senses.definitionCN: 演化出使生物更适合其环境的特征
senses.example: Over generations, the population adapted to the drier climate.
senses.exampleCN: 经过几代，这个种群适应了更干燥的气候。
senses.why: Biological adaptation happens over generations, not within a single lifetime.
senses.whyCN: 生物上的适应发生在几代之间，不是在单个生命里。

senses.title: To adjust a text, work or idea for a new audience
senses.titleCN: 调整文本、作品或想法以适应新受众
senses.definition: to modify a creative or intellectual work so it suits a different audience or medium
senses.definitionCN: 修改一部创造性或智识性作品，使其适合不同受众或媒介
senses.example: The novel was adapted to the screen only after major cuts were made.
senses.exampleCN: 这本小说经过大幅删改之后才被改编成电影。
senses.why: Here adapt borders on translate or rewrite, but with the sense of fitting to a new home.
senses.whyCN: 这里 adapt 接近翻译或重写，但带有「让它适合新家」的感觉。

senses.title: To respond flexibly to new information
senses.definition: to adjust one's beliefs or actions when new facts come in
senses.definitionCN: 当新事实进来时调整自己的信念或行动
senses.example: A good scientist adapts to new evidence rather than clinging to old theories.
senses.exampleCN: 好科学家会根据新证据调整自己，而不是抓住旧理论不放。
senses.why: Intellectual adaptation is close to change of mind, but with the sense of fitting better.
senses.whyCN: 智识上的适应接近改变想法，但带有「变得更合适」的意思。

senses.title: To make allowances for differences
senses.definition: to modify expectations or methods because someone's situation is different
senses.definitionCN: 因为某人的情况不同而修改预期或方法
senses.example: Teachers must adapt to the pace of each student in a mixed-ability class.
senses.exampleCN: 在混合能力班级里，老师必须适应每个学生的节奏。
senses.why: To adapt to others is to meet them part way, not to demand that they adapt only to you.
senses.whyCN: 适应他人就是向他们迈一步，而不是只要求他们向你迈。

senses.title: To become accustomed to or learn
senses.definition: to get used to something unfamiliar over time
senses.definitionCN: 随着时间过去，对不熟悉的东西变得习惯
senses.example: After a year he finally adapted to the long northern winters.
senses.exampleCN: 一年之后他终于习惯了漫长的北方冬天。
senses.why: This sense sits between change and mere habituation; the change may be small at first.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项介于改变和单纯习惯之间；最初的改变可能很小。

senses.title: To customize or tailor
senses.definition: to make something fit one particular person or purpose more closely
senses.definitionCN: 让某物更贴合某一特定的人或目的
senses.example: The software can be adapted to the exact needs of each client.
senses.exampleCN: 这个软件可以被定制以精确满足每个客户的需要。
senses.why: This sense is common in business: you adapt a product to a market niche.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项在商业中常见：你把一个产品调整到适合某个细分市场。

intro.en: Adapt comes from Latin adaptare, meaning to adjust or fit, built from ad- 'toward' and aptare 'to make fit' (from aptus 'fit'). English borrowed it in the sixteenth century.
intro.cn: adapt 来自拉丁语 adaptare「调整、使适合」，由 ad-「向」和 aptare「使适合」（来自 aptus「适合的」）构成。英语于十六世纪借入。

items.en: Adapt entered English in the sixteen-tens from Latin, first used in scientific and literary writing.
items.cn: adapt 于 1610 年代从拉丁语进入英语，最初用于科学和文学写作。

items.en: From ad- toward + aptare to make fit, a verb built on aptus fit or suited.
items.cn: 来自 ad-「向」+ aptare「使适合」，后者由 aptus「适合的」构成。

items.en: Aptus meant fit, suited or appropriate, the root of English apt and aptitude.
items.cn: aptus 意为「适合的、恰当的」，是英语 apt 和 aptitude 的词根。

items.en: The biological sense developed later, in the nineteenth century, under the influence of Darwinism.
items.cn: 生物义项后来才发展出来，在十九世纪达尔文主义影响下。

items.en: Today the phrase is used across personal growth, business, education, biology and technology.
items.cn: 今天这个短语用于个人成长、商业、教育、生物和技术等各个领域。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin root aptus 'fit'; the second group lists other ways of fitting something to a situation.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁词根 aptus「适合的」；第二组是把某物调整到适合某种情境的其他说法。

entries.definitionCN: 自然的能力或天赋，基于 aptus。

entries.definitionCN: 收养、采纳，虽然样子像但词根不同。

entries.definition: Skilled or expert, from the same root as adapt.
entries.definitionCN: 熟练的、内行的，来自 adapt 的同一词根。

entries.definition: Very close in meaning, slightly more about calibration.

entries.definition: A plain English phrase for the habituation sense, less formal.

entries.definition: To make one's behaviour fit a standard, more about rules than about growth.
entries.definitionCN: 让行为符合标准，更偏向规则而不是成长。

entries.definition: To customize closely for a particular purpose, close to the business sense.
entries.definitionCN: 为特定目的量身定制，接近商业上的义项。

entries.definition: To react to a situation, without necessarily implying lasting change.
entries.definitionCN: 对情境作出反应，不必然暗示持久改变。

abstract.en: Every species that still exists is a success story of adaptation.

senses.title: To regard something as caused by
senses.definition: to identify a cause or source for an event, result or state of affairs
senses.definitionCN: 为一个事件、结果或状态找出原因或来源
senses.example: Researchers attribute the decline in bee populations to widespread pesticide use.
senses.exampleCN: 研究人员把蜜蜂种群下降归因于广泛使用杀虫剂。
senses.why: The Latin root tribuere means to assign or give; attribute means to assign a cause to an effect.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 tribuere 意为「分配、给予」；attribute 就是把一个原因分配给一个结果。

senses.title: To regard a work or action as belonging to a person
senses.titleCN: 把作品或行为归属于某人
senses.definition: to assign authorship, agency or responsibility to a person
senses.definitionCN: 把作者身份、施动者或责任分配给某人
senses.example: Scholars now attribute the poem to a woman writing under a male name.
senses.exampleCN: 学者如今认为这首诗是一位用笔名的女性写的。
senses.why: Here attributing is a claim about who did it, not just what caused it.
senses.whyCN: 这里归因是关于「谁做的」的主张，而不只是「什么造成的」。

senses.title: To consider something a property or characteristic of
senses.definition: to treat a quality as a natural or inherent part of something
senses.definitionCN: 把一种性质当作某物天生或固有的一部分
senses.example: We often attribute creativity to the poet rather than to the culture that shaped the poet.
senses.exampleCN: 我们常常把创造力归为诗人个人的特质，而不是塑造了诗人的那个文化的。
senses.why: This sense is the noun attribute moving into verb form: assigning a property to a thing.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项是名词 attribute「属性」转为动词用法：把一个性质分配给某个东西。

senses.title: To assign blame or praise
senses.definition: to give responsibility for a good or bad outcome
senses.definitionCN: 为一个好或坏的结果分配责任
senses.example: Critics attribute the failure of the project to poor leadership.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者把项目的失败归因于糟糕的领导。
senses.why: Attributing blame is a social act: you're saying who or what should pay.
senses.whyCN: 归责是一个社会行为：你在说谁或什么该付出代价。

senses.title: To assign monetary value
senses.definition: to estimate a monetary value for something
senses.definitionCN: 为某物估算一个货币价值
senses.example: The insurance company attributed a value of two million pounds to the damaged painting.
senses.exampleCN: 保险公司给受损的画作估值两百万英镑。
senses.why: Here attributing is a matter of assigning a number, not a cause or a person.
senses.whyCN: 这里归因是分配一个数字的事，而不是一个原因或一个人的事。

senses.title: To explain behaviour or feelings as caused by
senses.titleCN: 把行为或感受解释为由……引起
senses.definition: to identify the psychological or social source of someone's behaviour
senses.definitionCN: 识别某人行为的心理或社会来源
senses.example: He attributes his fear of heights to a fall from a ladder when he was seven.
senses.exampleCN: 他把自己的恐高归因于七岁时从梯子上掉下来的经历。
senses.why: This sense is common in therapy and psychology, looking for the root of present reactions.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项在治疗和心理学里常见，寻找当下反应的根由。

senses.title: To treat as evidence of or proof of
senses.definition: to take something as an indication that something else is true
senses.definitionCN: 把某物当作另一事为真的指示
senses.example: Some historians attribute the style of these ruins to contact with Roman traders.
senses.exampleCN: 一些历史学家把这些遗址的风格归因于与罗马商人的接触。
senses.why: The passive form is common here: 'X is attributed to Y' means X is evidence for Y.
senses.whyCN: 被动形式在这里常用：X is attributed to Y 意味着 X 是 Y 的证据。

senses.title: To recognize or acknowledge
senses.definition: to acknowledge a quality, skill or contribution as real
senses.definitionCN: 承认一个性质、技能或贡献是真实的
senses.example: Even his opponents attribute intelligence to him.
senses.exampleCN: 甚至他的对手也承认他有才智。
senses.why: Here attributing is the act of granting a quality to someone publicly.
senses.whyCN: 这里归因就是公开把一个性质授予某人的行为。

intro.en: Attribute comes from Latin attribuere, to assign or give to, built from ad- 'to' and tribuere 'to assign'. English borrowed the verb in the sixteenth century.
intro.cn: attribute 来自拉丁语 attribuere「分配给」，由 ad-「向」和 tribuere「分配、给予」构成。英语于十六世纪借入。

items.en: Attribute entered English in the fifteen-forties, first used as a noun meaning an inherent quality.
items.cn: attribute 于 1540 年代进入英语，最初用作名词，指固有的性质。

items.en: Tribuere meant to assign, allot or pay out, the root of tribute, contribute, distribute, retribution.
items.cn: tribuere 意为「分配、分发、偿付」，是 tribute、contribute、distribute、retribution 的词根。

items.en: From ad- to + tribuere to assign, meaning to assign something to someone.
items.cn: 由 ad-「向」+ tribuere「分配」构成，意为「把某物分配给某人」。

items.en: The noun meaning an inherent quality developed alongside the verb meaning to assign.
items.cn: 名词（指固有的性质）与动词（指分配）的意思并列发展。

items.en: Today the phrase attribute to is most common in academic writing, journalism and psychological explanation.
items.cn: 今天 attribute to 这个短语在学术写作、新闻和心理学解释里最常见。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin root tribuere; the second group lists other ways of assigning a cause or quality to something.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁词根 tribuere；第二组是给某物分配原因或性质的其他说法。

normal.en: The root tribuere = to assign. So attribute = assign (to a cause or person).
normal.cn: 词根 tribuere = 分配。所以 attribute = 分配（给原因或人）。

normal.en: Detective on a case: attribute the crime to a suspect.
normal.cn: 侦探办案：把案件归因于一个嫌犯。

normal.en: The tribuere family: contribute, distribute, tribute, retribution — all about giving.
normal.cn: tribuere 家族：contribute、distribute、tribute、retribution——全都和「给」有关。

normal.en: Passive form is common: 'X is attributed to Y'.
normal.cn: 被动形式常见：X is attributed to Y。

abstract.en: Every attribution is an act of narrowing the infinite network of causes to one arrow.
abstract.cn: 每一次归因都是把无限的因果网络缩窄成一支箭。

abstract.en: Attributing is the mind's way of cutting the world into manageable pieces.
abstract.cn: 归因是心智把世界切分成可管理小块的方式。

abstract.en: To attribute too confidently is to forget that everything has many parents.
abstract.cn: 太自信地归因，就是忘记每件事都有很多父母。

examples.en: The rise in sea levels is attributed to both melting glaciers and thermal expansion.
examples.cn: 海平面上升被归因于冰川融化和海水热膨胀两方面。

examples.en: Scientists attribute much of the observed temperature increase to human greenhouse gas emissions.

examples.en: He attributed his recovery less to medicine than to his family's support.

senses.title: To be linked in the mind or experience
senses.definition: to be commonly thought of together, whether or not there is a logical connection
senses.definitionCN: 常被一起想到，不管逻辑上是否有关联
senses.example: Cats are often associated with independence, dogs with loyalty.
senses.exampleCN: 猫常被联想到独立，狗被联想到忠诚。
senses.why: The Latin root socius means companion; associated things are things that companion each other.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 socius 意为「同伴」；associated 的东西就是互相作伴的东西。

senses.title: To be statistically or causally linked
senses.titleCN: 在统计或因果上有联系
senses.definition: to appear together more often than chance would predict, or to have a causal relationship
senses.definitionCN: 出现频率比概率预测的更高，或者有因果关系
senses.example: Heavy alcohol use is strongly associated with liver disease.
senses.exampleCN: 大量饮酒与肝病之间有很强的统计学联系。
senses.why: Here association is not just mental — it is a real pattern in the data.
senses.whyCN: 这里的关联不只是心智上的——它是数据里的真实模式。

senses.title: To be a member or part of
senses.definition: to belong to a group, organization or category
senses.definitionCN: 属于一个团体、组织或类别
senses.example: Linguists associated with the university published the report.
senses.exampleCN: 与该大学有关联的语言学家发布了这份报告。
senses.why: This sense often uses the present participle: 'people associated with the project' = people who belong to it.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项常用现在分词：people associated with the project = 属于这个项目的人。

senses.title: To be historically or culturally linked
senses.titleCN: 在历史或文化上有联系
senses.definition: to have a historical or cultural connection, even if current links are weak
senses.definitionCN: 有历史或文化上的联系，即使当前的联系很弱
senses.example: The city is closely associated with the early life of the famous novelist.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市与那位著名小说家的早年生活密切相关。
senses.why: Historical association survives even when current facts no longer justify it.
senses.whyCN: 历史关联能在当前事实已经不再支持它的时候继续存在。

senses.title: To be connected in a chain or network
senses.definition: to stand as one node in a larger network of related items
senses.definitionCN: 作为更大的相关物品网络中的一个节点
senses.example: Every word is associated with thousands of other words through the brain's vocabulary network.
senses.exampleCN: 每个词都通过大脑的词汇网络与成千上万的其他词相连。
senses.why: Here association is a network link, not necessarily a direct two-way pair.
senses.whyCN: 这里的关联是网络里的一个链接，不必然是一个直接的双向配对。

senses.title: To be linked with a particular feeling or memory
senses.titleCN: 与某种情绪或记忆相连
senses.definition: to bring a feeling or memory to mind when encountered
senses.definitionCN: 遇到时能带来某种情绪或记忆
senses.example: The old street was associated with childhood summers in the minds of the villagers.
senses.exampleCN: 在村民心里，这条老街与童年夏天的记忆相连。
senses.why: This is the most personal sense of association: the thing that triggers the feeling.
senses.whyCN: 这是关联最个人化的义项：触发情绪的那个东西。

senses.title: To be considered together with as part of a pair
senses.definition: to be customarily mentioned together with something else
senses.definitionCN: 习惯上与其他东西一起被提到
senses.example: Romeo and Juliet are universally associated with young, forbidden love.
senses.exampleCN: 罗密欧与朱丽叶普遍被与年轻而被禁止的爱情联系在一起。
senses.why: Some associations are so strong that the pair is indivisible in popular thought.
senses.whyCN: 有些关联强到这一对在大众思维里不可分割。

senses.title: To be used or grouped together
senses.definition: to be found or used together, making up a set
senses.definitionCN: 一起被发现或使用，构成一个组合
senses.example: Salt and pepper are always associated with each other on dining tables.
senses.exampleCN: 盐和胡椒在餐桌上总是一起出现。
senses.why: This is the most concrete sense of association: things that are physically together.
senses.whyCN: 这是关联最具体的义项：实际上放在一起的东西。

intro.en: Associate comes from Latin associare, to unite with, built from ad- 'to' and sociare 'to join' (from socius 'companion'). The passive be associated with developed in English.
intro.cn: associate 来自拉丁语 associare「联合」，由 ad-「向」和 sociare「加入」（来自 socius「同伴」）构成。被动形式 be associated with 在英语中发展出来。

items.en: Associate entered English in the sixteenth century from Latin, first with the sense 'to join together'.
items.cn: associate 于十六世纪从拉丁语进入英语，最初义为「联合在一起」。

items.en: Socius meant companion or ally, a word that reached English as social, society, associate.
items.cn: socius 意为「同伴、盟友」，通过 social、society、associate 进入英语。

items.en: From ad- to + sociare to join, the verb meaning to unite with.
items.cn: 来自 ad-「向」+ sociare「加入」，意为「联合在一起」。

items.en: The passive construction 'to be associated' developed in English to describe connections without naming an agent.
items.cn: 被动结构 to be associated 在英语中发展出来，用来描述关系而不指明施动者。

items.en: The passive was later expanded into the phrasal verb be associated with, the form we use today.
items.cn: 被动形式后来扩展成 be associated with 这个短语动词，就是我们今天用的形式。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin root socius 'companion'; the second group lists other ways of saying two things are linked.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁词根 socius「同伴」；第二组是说两件事相连的其他方式。

normalIntro.cn: 想象两个人像同伴一样一起走——associated 的东西就是互相作伴。

normal.en: The Latin root is socius = companion. Associated things are companions.

normal.en: Socius gives social, society, sociology — the whole social world.

abstract.en: Associations are the mind's way of being lazy and smart at once.
abstract.cn: 联想是心智同时偷懒又聪明的方式。

abstract.en: Everything is associated with something else — nothing stands alone.
abstract.cn: 每一件事都和另一件事有关联——没有什么是孤立的。

abstract.en: The strength of an association measures how often two things have been seen together.
abstract.cn: 一个关联的强度，就是两件事一起被看到的频率。

examples.en: High levels of stress are associated with a weakened immune system.
examples.cn: 高水平压力与削弱的免疫系统之间有关联。

examples.en: For many people, the smell of wood smoke is associated with Christmas.
examples.cn: 对许多人来说，木柴烟味与圣诞节相连。

examples.en: This district has long been associated with artistic and literary life.
examples.cn: 这个区长时间以来一直与艺术和文学生活有关联。

branches.en: MENTAL LINK: the most common everyday use — one thing makes you think of the other.
branches.cn: 心智关联：最常见的日常用法——一件事让你想到另一件。

branches.en: CAUSAL OR STATISTICAL LINK: the scientific use, where association means correlation.
branches.cn: 因果或统计关联：科学用法，此时 association 意为相关。

branches.en: BELONGING TO A GROUP: people associated with a project are part of it.
branches.cn: 属于一个团体：与项目有关联的人就是项目的一部分。

branches.en: HISTORICAL AND MEMORY LINKS: associations that survive even when facts change.
branches.cn: 历史与记忆关联：即使事实变了仍然存活的关联。

branches.en: NETWORK, FEELING, PAIRING, PHYSICAL CO-OCCURRENCE: the softer and more concrete uses.
branches.cn: 网络、情绪、配对、物理共现：更温和或更具体的用法。

intro.en: Be associated with is built on Latin associare: ad- to, sociare to join, from socius companion. The passive voice with be + past participle lets us describe connections without naming who joined them.

senses.title: To have something as a typical feature
senses.definition: to display a feature that is usual or representative of the thing being described
senses.definitionCN: 展示某种对于被描述对象来说常见或有代表性的特征
senses.example: Deserts are characterized by very low rainfall.
senses.exampleCN: 沙漠以极低的降雨量为特征。
senses.why: The Greek root kharakter meant an engraved mark, a signature that tells you what a thing is.
senses.whyCN: 希腊词根 kharakter 意为「刻痕、签名」——告诉你一件事是什么东西的记号。

senses.title: To have something as a defining feature
senses.definition: to display a feature that distinguishes this thing from similar things
senses.definitionCN: 展示一种把此物与类似事物区分开的特征
senses.example: Sonatas are characterized by their typical three-movement structure.
senses.exampleCN: 奏鸣曲以其典型的三乐章结构为界定性特征。
senses.why: Here characterized means 'you can recognize it by this feature'.
senses.whyCN: 这里 characterized 的意思是「你可以用这个特征来认出它」。

senses.title: To have a particular mood or quality
senses.definition: to display an overall tone or atmosphere
senses.definitionCN: 展示一种整体的语调或氛围
senses.example: The writer's early novels are characterized by an air of melancholy.
senses.exampleCN: 这位作家的早期小说带有一种忧郁的氛围。
senses.why: Features can be intangible too — a mood is as much a characteristic as a shape.
senses.whyCN: 特征也可以是无形的——一种情绪和一种形状一样，都是特征。

senses.title: To be described or portrayed as
senses.definition: to be given a particular description or representation in art or writing
senses.definitionCN: 在艺术或文字中被给予某种描述或表现
senses.example: The god Zeus is characterized as both wise and impulsive in Greek myths.
senses.exampleCN: 在希腊神话里，宙斯被刻画得既智慧又冲动。
senses.why: This sense overlaps with the verb characterize: the passive form says that someone has drawn the portrait.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项与动词 characterize 重叠：被动形式表示有人画了这幅肖像。

senses.title: To be marked by
senses.definition: to show signs or traces of something
senses.definitionCN: 显示某物的痕迹或迹象
senses.example: The fossil bone is characterized by several deep scratch marks.
senses.exampleCN: 这块化石骨头上带有几条深深的划痕。
senses.why: The scratches are a visible signature on the bone — just as the root kharakter meant an engraved mark.
senses.whyCN: 这些划痕就是骨头上看得见的签名——正如词根 kharakter 本意是刻痕。

senses.title: To have a dominant trait in common
senses.definition: to share a prominent feature that runs through the whole group or period
senses.definitionCN: 共有一个贯穿整个群体或时期的突出特征
senses.example: The twentieth century was characterized by two world wars and rapid industrialization.
senses.exampleCN: 二十世纪的主要特征是两次世界大战和快速工业化。
senses.why: Here characterized points to the largest-scale features of an era.
senses.whyCN: 这里 characterized 指向一个时代最大尺度上的特征。

senses.title: To be represented in a particular way
senses.definition: to stand for or symbolize something larger
senses.definitionCN: 代表或象征某个更大的东西
senses.example: The dove is often characterized by the olive branch it carries in its beak.
senses.exampleCN: 鸽子嘴里叼着橄榄枝，这常被用来象征和平。
senses.why: The feature stands for something beyond itself — a sign or symbol.
senses.whyCN: 这个特征代表了它自身之外的东西——一个记号或象征。

senses.title: To have a certain tendency or bias
senses.definition: to display a regular or typical tendency in behaviour or thought
senses.definitionCN: 在行为或思维上表现出稳定或典型的倾向
senses.example: The approach is characterized by a strong preference for empirical evidence.
senses.exampleCN: 这种方法的特点是强烈偏好经验证据。
senses.why: This sense is common in academic writing, describing a method's built-in assumptions.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项在学术写作中常见，用来描述一种方法的内置假设。

intro.en: Characterize comes from character, which enters English through Latin from Greek kharakter, meaning an engraved mark or impressed sign. The verb suffix -ize turns the noun into an action: to make such a mark on something.
intro.cn: characterize 来自 character，后者经拉丁语从希腊语 kharakter「刻痕、印记」进入英语。动词后缀 -ize 把名词变成动作：在某物上刻这样一个记号。

items.en: Characterize was coined as a verb in the seventeen-nineties, built from character.
items.cn: characterize 作为动词造于 1790 年代，由 character 构成。

items.en: Kharakter meant an engraved mark, a stylus for engraving, or a distinguishing mark.
items.cn: kharakter 意为「刻痕、刻刀、可辨别的记号」。

items.en: Latin borrowed kharakter as character, which meant a distinctive mark or impressed image.
items.cn: 拉丁语把 kharakter 借为 character，指可辨认的记号或刻印的图像。

items.en: In English character broadened from a mark to a person's qualities, then to the qualities of anything.
items.cn: 在英语里 character 从「记号」扩展为人的品质，再扩展为任何事物的品质。

items.en: The suffix -ize turns a noun into an action: to mark something with a characteristic.
items.cn: 后缀 -ize 把名词变成动作：给某物刻上一个特征记号。

note.en: The first group shares the root kharakter; the second group lists other ways of describing a typical feature.
note.cn: 第一组共享词根 kharakter；第二组是描述典型特征的其他方式。

entries.definition: Slightly more subjective, about what people say about something.

entries.definition: To be particularly noticeable on account of.
entries.definitionCN: 因……而特别显眼。

entries.definition: A plain way of saying something has a feature.

entries.definition: Very close to be characterized by, emphasizing contrast with others.

normalIntro.en: Break it down: character = an engraved mark; -ize = to make. So characterize = to mark something with its distinguishing feature.
normalIntro.cn: 拆开看：character = 刻痕、记号；-ize = 使成为。所以 characterize = 用它的可辨别特征给它刻上记号。

normal.en: Desert = low rainfall characteristic: you can read it from the signature.
normal.cn: 沙漠 = 低降雨量特征：你能从签名上读出来。

normal.en: Root kharakter = engraved mark, stylus. A mark that tells you what the thing is.
normal.cn: 词根 kharakter = 刻痕、刻刀。告诉你这个东西是什么的标记。

normal.en: Characterize = give a character mark to something.
normal.cn: characterize = 给某物刻上一个 characteristic 记号。

normal.en: The passive be characterized by is the most common form.
normal.cn: 被动形式 be characterized by 是最常见的用法。

normal.en: Characterize was coined in the 1790s from character.
normal.cn: characterize 是 1790 年代由 character 新造的词。

abstract.en: To characterize is to give a thing its signature, the mark that lets you pick it out of a crowd.
abstract.cn: characterize 就是给一件东西它的签名——让你能从人群里把它挑出来的记号。

abstract.en: Every characterization is a choice: which mark matters enough to be the signature?
abstract.cn: 每一次刻画都是一个选择：哪个记号足够重要，能当上签名？

abstract.en: The strongest characteristic is the one you'd draw first in a sketch.
abstract.cn: 最强的特征，就是你在素描里会先画的那一笔。

examples.en: Urban areas are characterized by high population density and many tall buildings.
examples.cn: 城市地区的特点是高人口密度和许多高楼。

examples.en: The 1960s were characterized by rapid social change and new political movements.
examples.cn: 二十世纪六十年代的主要特征是快速的社会变化和新的政治运动。

examples.en: Good scientific writing is characterized by precision, clarity and careful argumentation.
examples.cn: 好的科学写作以精确、清晰和严谨的论证为特征。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「比 卡瑞克特瑞兹的 拜」——「卡瑞克特」刻记号，「瑞兹」让发生：让某物刻上自己的特征记号，就是以……为特征

root: 希腊语 kharakter（来自 kharax「尖头棍」）→ 拉丁语 character「刻痕、记号」→ 英语 character「特征；人物」→ 动词 characterize（1790 年代由 character + -ize 构成）；被动形式 be characterized by 在英语内部发展；同词根 family 包括 characteristic、charisma、charge 等。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses range from having something as a typical feature, to a defining feature, to a mood or quality, to being described or portrayed, to being marked by visible signs, to shared features of an era, to symbolic representation, to having a built-in tendency or bias.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从「某物作为典型特征」出发，依次走向「界定性特征」、「情绪或气质」、「被描绘或刻画」、「被可见痕迹标记」、「一个时代的共有特征」、「象征性表现」与「内置倾向或偏向」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stylus engraving a distinctive mark on a wax seal, the signature of what the object is.
core.cn: 核心意象：一支刻刀在蜡封上刻出独特的标记——这个物件是什么东西的签名。

branches.en: TYPICAL AND DEFINING FEATURES: the core use — marking the thing's signature.
branches.cn: 典型与界定性特征：核心用法——给东西刻上签名。

branches.en: MOOD, PORTRAYAL AND ART: softer uses where the mark is less tangible.
branches.cn: 情绪、刻画与艺术：更温和的用法，标记不那么有形。

branches.en: VISIBLE TRACES: the most literal use of the root — a real mark on the object.
branches.cn: 可见痕迹：词根最字面的用法——物件上真的有个刻痕。

branches.en: ERA-SCALE FEATURES: applying the marking to a whole period.
branches.cn: 时代尺度特征：把标记用在整个时期上。

branches.en: SYMBOLIC AND METHOD BIAS: the uses furthest from the original engraving.
branches.cn: 象征与方法偏向：离最初刻痕最远的用法。

intro.en: Be characterized by is built on the verb characterize, which combines the Greek-derived noun character with the verb suffix -ize. The root kharakter meant an engraved mark.
intro.cn: be characterized by 建立在动词 characterize 上，后者把来自希腊语的名词 character 和动词后缀 -ize 结合起来。词根 kharakter 意为「刻痕」。

latinIntro.en: The Greek root is kharakter, from kharax 'pointed stick'. Latin borrowed it as character, keeping the sense of a distinguishing mark.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊词根是 kharakter，来自 kharax「尖头棍」。拉丁语借为 character，保留了「可辨别记号」的意思。

senses.title: To be made up of physical parts or elements
senses.titleCN: 由物理部件或元素构成
senses.definition: to consist of particular tangible or material components
senses.definitionCN: 由特定有形或物质成分构成
senses.example: Water is composed of two atoms of hydrogen and one of oxygen.
senses.exampleCN: 水由两个氢原子和一个氧原子构成。
senses.why: The Latin root ponere means to put; componere means to put together, so composed things have been put together from parts.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 ponere 意为「放」；componere 意为「放在一起」，所以 composed 的东西是由各部分放在一起形成的。

senses.title: To be formed from non-physical parts
senses.definition: to be made up of ideas, feelings, qualities or abstract elements
senses.definitionCN: 由想法、情感、品质或抽象元素构成
senses.example: Her personality is composed of shyness, curiosity and a sharp sense of humour.
senses.exampleCN: 她的性格由害羞、好奇心和敏锐的幽默感构成。
senses.why: The parts don't have to be tangible — an abstract quality can be a component.
senses.whyCN: 部分不必有形——抽象品质也可以是一个成分。

senses.title: To be organized into parts
senses.definition: to have a structure made up of organized sections or units
senses.definitionCN: 有一个由组织过的部分或单元构成的结构
senses.example: The committee is composed of representatives from each department.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会由每个部门的代表组成。
senses.why: Here composition is about organization as well as material: the parts have been deliberately arranged.
senses.whyCN: 这里 composition 既关乎材料也关乎组织：各部分被有意安排过。

senses.title: To be made up of a mixture
senses.definition: to consist of a blend of different substances or ingredients
senses.definitionCN: 由不同物质或配料的混合物构成
senses.example: The alloy is composed of copper, zinc and a small amount of tin.
senses.exampleCN: 这种合金由铜、锌和少量锡构成。
senses.why: Mixtures are one common kind of composition, but composition can also be pure one thing.
senses.whyCN: 混合物是 composition 的一种常见形式，但 composition 也可以是纯的一样东西。

senses.title: To be put together by an author or composer
senses.definition: to have been assembled deliberately by a creative person
senses.definitionCN: 由一个创作者有意地拼装起来
senses.example: The symphony is composed of four movements, each with its own character.
senses.exampleCN: 这部交响曲由四个乐章组成，每个乐章都有自己的性格。
senses.why: Here the sense overlaps with the artistic act of composing music or writing.
senses.whyCN: 这里的义项与创作音乐或写作的 compose 行为重叠。

senses.title: To be calm and well-put-together (discrepant sense)
senses.titleCN: 沉着冷静（与前面不同的义项）
senses.definition: to be calm and self-controlled
senses.definitionCN: 平静且自控良好
senses.example: She spoke in a composed voice despite the shouting around her.
senses.exampleCN: 尽管周围在喊叫，她还是用沉着的声音说话。
senses.why: This is a different use of the participle composed: a composed person has their emotions put in place, not scattered.
senses.whyCN: 这是 composed 分词的另一个用法：一个 composed 的人把情绪都放对了地方，没有散掉。

senses.title: To be made up of different genres or styles
senses.titleCN: 由不同风格或流派构成
senses.definition: to combine features from several distinct traditions
senses.definitionCN: 结合了几种不同传统的特征
senses.example: The film is composed of equal parts thriller, romance and dark comedy.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影由惊悚、爱情和黑色喜剧三种成分平均构成。
senses.why: Works can be composed of styles just as bodies are composed of cells.
senses.whyCN: 作品可以由风格构成，正如身体由细胞构成。

senses.title: To be formed by combining groups or populations
senses.titleCN: 由群体或种群合并而成
senses.definition: to be made up of different social or biological groups
senses.definitionCN: 由不同社会或生物群体构成
senses.example: Modern Brazil is composed of Indigenous peoples, descendants of European settlers and African descendants.
senses.exampleCN: 现代巴西由原住民、欧洲殖民者后代和非洲后裔构成。
senses.why: Demographic composition is a major use of the phrase in social science.
senses.whyCN: 人口构成是社会科学里这个短语的一大用法。

intro.en: Be composed of comes from Latin componere, to put together, from com- 'together' and ponere 'to put'. The passive participle composed entered English in the fourteenth century.
intro.cn: be composed of 来自拉丁语 componere「放在一起」，由 com-「一起」和 ponere「放置」构成。被动分词 composed 于十四世纪进入英语。

items.en: Compose entered English in the fourteenth century, borrowed from Old French composer which itself combined Latin componere and ponere.
items.cn: compose 于十四世纪进入英语，借自古法语 composer，后者结合了拉丁语 componere 与 ponere。

items.en: Ponere meant to put, place or set, a root that reaches position, deposit, dispose, expose, impose, oppose, propose, suppose.
items.cn: ponere 意为「放、放置」，词根包括 position、deposit、dispose、expose、impose、oppose、propose、suppose。

items.en: From com- together + ponere to put, the verb to put together or arrange.
items.cn: 由 com-「一起」+ ponere「放」构成，意为「放在一起、安排」。

items.en: The passive participle composed developed the sense 'calm and self-possessed' by the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 被动分词 composed 到十七世纪发展出「沉着、自控」的意思。

items.en: The phrasal verb be composed of became the standard way to describe composition from the nineteenth century.
items.cn: be composed of 这个短语到十九世纪成为描述构成的标准方式。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin root ponere 'to put'; the second group lists other ways of saying what something is made of.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁词根 ponere「放」；第二组是表达某物由什么构成的其他说法。

entries.definition: To put together, as in compose a letter or compose music.
entries.definitionCN: 放在一起，如 compose a letter 或 compose music。

entries.definition: A place where something has been put.
entries.definitionCN: 某物被放置的位置。

entries.definition: Something put down, especially money or sediment.
entries.definitionCN: 被放下的东西，尤其是钱或沉积物。

entries.definition: To put something out in the open.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物放到外面。

entries.definition: To put oneself against something.
entries.definitionCN: 把自己放在某物的对面。

entries.definition: A very common plain English way of saying the same thing.
entries.definitionCN: 表示同样意思的非常常见的日常说法。

entries.definition: Very close in meaning, slightly less formal than be composed of.
entries.definitionCN: 意思非常接近，比 be composed of 略不太正式。

entries.definition: To include or consist of, a single verb without be or of.
entries.definitionCN: 包括或由……构成，是一个不需要 be 或 of 的单词。

entries.definition: A more formal synonym for be composed of.
entries.definitionCN: be composed of 的更正式同义词。

entries.definition: Slightly more concrete, suggesting actual construction from materials.
entries.definitionCN: 略更具体，暗示从材料实际建造。

normalIntro.en: Think of it as put together: com- = together, ponere = put. So composed = put together from parts.
normalIntro.cn: 把它想成「放在一起」：com- = 一起，ponere = 放。所以 composed = 由各部分放在一起形成。

normal.en: com- (together) + ponere (put) = put together.
normal.cn: com-（一起）+ ponere（放）= 放在一起。

normal.en: H2O is composed of 2 H and 1 O — chemistry textbook example.
normal.cn: H2O 由 2 个 H 和 1 个 O 构成——化学课本例子。

normal.en: The huge ponere family: position, deposit, expose, oppose, propose, suppose.
normal.cn: 庞大的 ponere 家族：position、deposit、expose、oppose、propose、suppose。

normal.en: Composed also means calm — a composed person has emotions put in place.
normal.cn: composed 还有「沉着」的意思——composed 的人情绪都放对了地方。

normal.en: Compose entered English in the 14C.
normal.cn: compose 于十四世纪进入英语。

abstract.en: Everything composed is a sum of smaller choices about what to put next to what.
abstract.cn: 每一个 composed 的东西，都是一串关于「把什么放在什么旁边」的小选择之和。

abstract.en: A composed personality is also composed — emotions arranged in the right positions.
abstract.cn: 沉着的性格也是 composed 的——情绪被放在了正确的位置上。

abstract.en: From atoms to nations, every level of organization is an act of composition.
abstract.cn: 从原子到国家，每一层组织都是一次 composition 行为。

examples.en: The human genome is composed of approximately three billion base pairs.
examples.cn: 人类基因组由大约三十亿个碱基对组成。

examples.en: The company's workforce is composed of engineers, designers and project managers.
examples.cn: 这家公司的员工由工程师、设计师和项目经理组成。

examples.en: A typical medieval diet was composed mainly of grains, vegetables and dairy products.
examples.cn: 典型的中世纪饮食主要由谷物、蔬菜和乳制品构成。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a mosaic where each tiny tile has been deliberately placed beside its neighbours to form a larger image.
core.cn: 核心意象：一幅马赛克，每一块小瓷片都被有意地放在相邻位置，共同构成更大的图像。

branches.en: PHYSICAL COMPOSITION: the clearest and most common use.
branches.cn: 物理构成：最清楚、最常见的用法。

branches.en: ABSTRACT AND ORGANIZED PARTS: qualities and groups treated as put-together components.
branches.cn: 抽象与有组织部分：品质和群体都被当作放在一起的成分。

branches.en: MIXTURES: a special case where the parts blend rather than form a clear structure.
branches.cn: 混合物：各部分混合而非形成清晰结构的特殊情况。

branches.en: ARTISTIC AND DIVERGENT SENSE: deliberately composed art vs. calm self-possession.
branches.cn: 艺术与分裂义项：有意创作的艺术 vs 沉着冷静。

branches.en: STYLES AND DEMOGRAPHICS: composition applied to cultural and social wholes.
branches.cn: 风格与人口统计：composition 用到文化和社会整体上。

intro.en: Be composed of is built on the Latin root ponere 'to put', with com- marking that things are put together. The passive participle lets us describe what something is made of without naming who put it together.
intro.cn: be composed of 建立在拉丁词根 ponere「放」上，com- 标记「放在一起」。被动分词让我们可以不指明谁把东西放在一起，只说它由什么构成。
